660.1: Raag Dhanasari, Ghar 1, Chaupade, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). There is one God, Ik Oankar, the One who pervades all and is ever the same; his Name is Sat (the One who truly is); he is the Creator, the Being who dwells in all, without fear, without enmity, his form beyond time, unborn, self-existent, realised by the Guru's grace. My own soul is afraid; to whom shall I cry out? I have served the one who makes sorrow forgotten, the Giver for ever and ever. My Master is ever new; he is the Giver for ever and ever. Night and day let us serve the Master; in the end it is he who sets us free. Hearing (his Name) again and again, O my soul-bride, one is carried across. O Merciful One, may I cross over through your Name; I am for ever a sacrifice (to you). The One True Lord is in every place; there is none besides him. Only the one on whom he casts his glance of grace serves him. Without you, O Beloved, how can I live? Grant me that greatness by which I may stay attached to your Name. O Beloved, there is no one else before whom I could go and say it. I serve my own Master; I beg of no one else. Nanak is his servant, and moment by moment he is offered up to him, piece by piece. O Master, moment by moment (Nanak) is offered up to your Name, piece by piece. ॥4॥
Chaupade (chau, four; pad, stanza): hymns of four stanzas.
Each of the four stanzas of this shabad is followed by a Rahao line of its own.
660.2: Raag Dhanasari, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). We humans are of a single breath; we know neither the term (of our life) nor the moment (of death). Nanak prays: serve him alone to whom the soul and the breath of life belong. O blind one, consider and see: how many days does (this) life last? (O Lord,) breath, flesh, soul, all are yours; you are deeply dear to me. Thus says Nanak, the poet, O True Sustainer. If you give nothing to someone, O my Master, what can he bring out to offer as a pledge? Nanak prays: one receives just that which is due by what was written before. The deceitful one did not keep the Master's Name in his mind; he practised deceit. When he was seized and driven to the door of Jam (the messenger of Death), then he went, repenting. As long as we remain in the world, O Nanak, let us hear something (of the Lord) and say something. We have searched to weariness and found no lasting stay (here); let us live as those who have died while yet alive. ॥5॥
To die while alive: to die to Haumai (ego) and to worldly desire while still living in the body.
661.1: Raag Dhanasari, Ghar 2, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. How shall I remember him? (By my own effort) he cannot be remembered. (Without him) my heart burns, and my soul cries out in pain. That True One himself creates and adorns; if he is forgotten, how can any good come? He is not found by cleverness or by giving orders; how, then, may I meet the True One, O my mother? Only a rare one goes to look at the merchandise of the Naam (the Name, God's presence remembered); none tastes it, none eats it. Winning people over brings no honour; honour stays only when he himself preserves it. Wherever I look, there he is, pervading. (O Lord,) apart from you there is no other place. If anyone tries (by his own effort), what comes of his doing? (it comes to) the one on whom that True One bestows it. Soon (I) must rise and depart, in a moment or in a single beat of time; what face shall I show? I have no virtues with me. As is the glance he casts, so does one become; without the glance of his grace, O Nanak, none is anything. ॥4॥
661.2: Raag Dhanasari, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). When (God) casts his glance of grace, then he can be remembered; (then) the soul melts and (one) stays attuned (to him) in loving attention. One makes the soul and the Supreme Soul one, and the duality within dies within. By the Guru's grace (God) is found; when the mind is attached to the Lord, death devours (one) no more. When the True One is remembered, light dawns (within), and by it one remains detached even in the midst of the poison (of Maya). Such is the greatness of the True Guru that among sons and wife one attains the highest state. The servant does such service that he lays his soul before him whose it is. He who pleases the Master is accepted; that servant receives honour in the Lord's court. The servant who enshrines the True Guru's form in his heart obtains whatever fruit he desires. The True Master shows him mercy; why should such a servant fear Jam? Says Nanak, when one reflects (on the Word) and enshrines love for the true Bani, only then does one find the door of liberation. This Shabad is all chanting and austerity; it is the most excellent. ॥5॥
Dubidha (duality): the divided mind, which loves another besides God.
The True Guru's form (moorat): in Gurbani the Guru's form is his Word, the Shabad (the Darpan: the Guru's spiritual form, his Bani).
661.3: Raag Dhanasari, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). The soul burns again and again; burning and burning, it wears itself away in so many vices. The body in which the (Lord's) Bani is forgotten wails like one sick with a chronic disease. Much speaking is mere babbling; without our speaking, he knows everything. He who made the ears, the eyes and the nose, who gave the tongue that speaks so swiftly, who placed the mind in the fire (of the womb) and kept it safe, (by whose power) the breath moves and one speaks in every place: (he is the one to remember). All the attachment, the loves and the relishes (of the world) are blackness, all of them, stain upon stain. With the stains of faults on his face one departs, and in the Lord's court there is no place for him to sit. (O Lord,) only by (your) grace is the uttering of your Name received; holding to it one crosses over; there is no other place. Even if one is drowning, care is still taken of him (through the Name). O Nanak, the True One gives to all. ॥4॥
662.1: Raag Dhanasari, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). If a thief offers praise, the heart is not moved; if he speaks ill, (one) is not diminished by a hair. No one stands surety for a thief. How can one who is marked a thief be (taken for) good? Listen, O blind mind, greedy as a dog, O false one: without a word spoken, the true are recognised. A thief may be handsome, a thief may be clever, yet the counterfeit is worth no more than a dugana (a trifling coin). If it is kept alongside (the genuine) and mixed in with them, when it is tested, it proves false. As one does, so one receives; one sows and oneself eats (the harvest). If one keeps singing one's own praises, (one does not become great by it); as is one's inclination, so is the road one takes. Though one may tell a hundred lies, falsehood and rubbish, and though the whole world may call him (good), (O Lord,) if it pleases you, the simple one is accepted. O Nanak, the Knower, the all-wise, knows (all). ॥4॥
662.2: Raag Dhanasari, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). The body is the paper, and the mind the decree (written on it); the ignorant one does not read the writ upon his head. In the Lord's court three (kinds of) writ are engraved; see, the false one is of no use. O Nanak, if there is silver in (the coin), everyone calls it genuine, genuine. The qazi speaks falsehood and eats filth (ill-gotten gain); the Brahmin takes his holy bath after slaying living beings; the yogi, blind, does not know the way: all three lay the groundwork of ruin. He alone is a yogi who recognises the way and, by the Guru's grace, knows the One. He is a qazi who turns (his mind) back (from the world) and, by the Guru's grace, dies while living. He is a Brahmin who reflects on Brahm (God); he himself swims across and carries all his families across. He alone is wise who washes his heart clean; he alone is a Muslim who rids himself of filth. The learned one who understands is accepted, he upon whose head is the mark of the Lord's court. ॥4॥
The three writs: by the Darpan, the records of deeds done under the three qualities (gunas) of Maya, rajas, tamas and sattva.
Qazi: the Muslim judge, who also taught the law of Islam.
662.3: Raag Dhanasari, Ghar 3, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. It is not that age now; there is no yoga, nor any way of truth; the world's places of worship have been defiled; in this way the world is drowning. In Kalyug the Name of Ram is the most excellent of all. They shut their eyes and hold their noses, (but all) to cheat the world. They pinch their noses with thumb and fingers (and claim) they see the three worlds; yet they see nothing of what lies behind their backs: this is a strange lotus posture. The Kshatriyas have abandoned their dharma and taken up the language of the mlechhas; the whole world has become of one varna, and the order of dharma has come to an end. (The pandits) compose the eight (works of grammar), study the Puranas and practise the Vedas; (but) says servant Nanak: without the Lord's Name there is no liberation. ॥4॥
Kalyug: in the reckoning of the Puranas, the fourth and darkest of the world's four ages, held to be the present one.
Padam asan: the lotus posture of yoga, sitting cross-legged with each foot upon the opposite thigh.
Mlechh: impure, alien; the caste Hindus' word for foreigners, here the Muslim rulers of the time. Varna: the four caste orders of Hindu society.
The eight (asht saaj): works of grammar; by the Faridkot Teeka the eight grammars composed by the rishis, by the Darpan works such as Panini's Ashtadhyayi (eight chapters).
663.1: Raag Dhanasari, Aarti, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. The sky is the platter; the sun and the moon are its lamps, and the clusters of stars are like pearls; the sandal-scented breeze from the Malaya hills is the incense, the wind waves the fly-whisk, and all the plant life blossoms for the Light (that is God). What a wondrous aarti this is! O Destroyer of the round of births, this is your aarti: the unstruck sound resounds as its drums. Thousands are your eyes, yet you have no eye; thousands are your forms, yet not one form is yours; thousands are your spotless feet, yet you have not one foot; you are without a nose, yet thousands are your noses: these wonders of yours have enchanted me. Within all is the light, and that light is he. By his radiance there is light within all. Through the Guru's teaching this light becomes manifest. Whatever pleases him, that becomes the aarti. My mind is lured by the nectar of the Lord's lotus feet; night and day I thirst for it. Give Nanak, the rain-bird, the water of your grace, by which he may abide in your Name. ॥4॥

Aarti is the worship in which a platter of lamps, incense and flowers is waved before an image; in this shabad all of nature performs the Creator's aarti. Malaanalo (malaya + anila, wind) is the fragrant breeze from the sandalwood hills of Malaya in the south of India; the fly-whisk (chaur) is waved over one who is revered.
The Anhad (anāhata, unstruck) Shabad is the sound made by no striking: the divine music that sounds unbroken through all creation.
The saaring (papiha, the rain-bird) is said to drink only drops of rain, and to keep calling out for them.
663.2: Raag Dhanasari, Ghar 2, Chaupade, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. This wealth (of the Name) is inexhaustible; it neither runs out nor is lost. The perfect True Guru has shown it (to me). To my own True Guru I am ever a sacrifice; by the Guru's grace I enshrine the Lord in my mind. They alone are rich who attune their love to the Name of the Lord; the Perfect Guru has revealed the Lord's wealth (within them); by the Lord's grace it comes to dwell in the mind. Failings are cut away and virtues settle in the heart through the Perfect Guru, in Sahaj and in love. The true Bani of the Perfect Guru brings peace within the mind, and settles (there) in Sahaj. Behold one wonder, O people, O brothers: slaying duality, (the Guru) enshrines the Lord in the mind. The Naam is priceless; it cannot be obtained (at any price); by the Guru's grace it comes to dwell in the mind. The One God dwells in all; through the Guru's teaching he becomes manifest in the heart. One who, in Sahaj, has known God and recognised him, O Nanak, receives the Naam, and (his) mind is content. ॥4॥
664.1: Raag Dhanasari, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). The wealth of the Lord's Name is pure and utterly boundless; through the Guru's Shabad its storehouses are filled. Know that all else but the wealth of the Naam is poison; in attachment to Maya the proud one burns. Some rare one, through the Guru, tastes the Lord's sweet essence; he is in bliss always, day and night; (this essence) is attained by perfect fortune. The Shabad is a lamp, shining in the three worlds; whoever tastes it becomes pure. With the pure Naam he washes off the filth of Haumai, and through true devotion there is peace for ever. One who has tasted the Lord's sweet essence is the Lord's servant; he has joy always, and never sorrow. He himself is liberated, and he has others liberated too; he repeats the Lord's Name, and from the Lord he receives peace. Without the True Guru the whole (world) has died wailing; night and day they burn, and (none) finds calm. When the True Guru is met, he quenches all craving; O Nanak, through the Naam one finds calm and peace. ॥4॥
Haumai (I-am-ness): the sense of a self apart from God.
664.2: Raag Dhanasari, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). The Naam is wealth for ever: cherish it within you, (the Name of the One) who alone sustains all beings and creatures. The treasure of liberation comes to those who, attuning their love, stay dyed in the Lord's Name. By serving the Guru one gains the wealth that is the Lord's Name; there is light within (him), and he meditates on the Lord's Name. This deep dye of the Lord, the Husband, comes upon the soul-bride who has made peace her adornment; she enjoys that God. In Haumai no one finds God; strayed from the Root, one wastes one's life. From the Guru, through the Bani, come calm and the peace of Sahaj; true is (the Guru's) service, and through it one merges in the Naam. Through the Shabad the Beloved is met, (and one) meditates on him ever; through the True Name (one) receives glory. The Creator himself is present, age after age; when he casts his glance of grace, union (with him) comes about. Through Gurbani one enshrines the Lord in the mind; O Nanak, those dyed in the True One, God himself has united (with himself). ॥4॥
664.3: Raag Dhanasari, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). The world is soiled, and grows ever more soiled; lured by another (than God), it comes and goes. In the love of another all people are being ruined; the manmukh suffers blows, and has lost his honour. Through serving the Guru one becomes pure; the Naam dwells within, and (one's) honour is exalted. The Gurmukhs are saved in the Lord's refuge; dyed in the Lord's Name, they have made devotion firm (in their hearts). One who performs devotion receives glory; dyed in the True One, they stay merged in peace and Sahaj. Know that a buyer of the True One is rare; (such a one) recognises his own self through the Guru's Shabad. True is (his) capital, true (his) trade; blessed is the person who has love for the Naam. That True God has attached some to the Truth; (to them) he makes the sublime Bani, the Shabad, heard. True is the service of the True God; O Nanak, through the Name he is the one who adorns (all). ॥4॥
665.1: Raag Dhanasari, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). To those who serve the Lord I am a sacrifice; in their hearts is the Truth, and on their lips the True Name. Cherish the True One, the True One alone, and sorrow departs; through the true Shabad he comes to dwell in the mind. Hearing Gurbani, one washes away (one's) filth, and in Sahaj enshrines the Lord's Name in the mind. He quenches falsehood, deceit and the fire of craving, and finds calm within, and peace in Sahaj. If one walks in the Guru's will, then self-conceit departs; singing the Lord's praises, one finds the true mansion (of his presence). One who neither understands the Shabad nor knows the Bani: that blind manmukh's (life) passes in pain. If one meets the True Guru, then one finds peace, and holds Haumai in check within. To whom else should one speak? That One alone is the Giver; when he shows grace, union comes about through the Shabad. Having met the Beloved (Guru), may I sing the True One's praises; may Nanak, becoming true, be pleasing to the True One. ॥4॥
665.2: Raag Dhanasari, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). When the mind dies (to self), its wandering dies away; without the mind dying, how can one find the Lord? Rare is the one who knows the medicine by which this mind dies; the mind dies through the Shabad: that one alone understands this. The one whom the Lord forgives, he grants the glory that, by the Guru's grace, he comes to dwell in the mind. When, through the Guru, one practises the conduct worth practising, then one comes to understand this mind. The mind is drunk, like an elephant maddened by wine; the Guru, striking it with the goad, brings it to life. The mind is hard to tame; some rare one tames it. When one consumes what will not yield (the mind's stubbornness), then (the mind) becomes pure. Through the Guru, one has set this mind in order, and casts Haumai and the vices out from within. Those whom he has, from the very beginning, kept joined in his union are never parted (from him); they stay merged in the Shabad. God himself knows his own power; O Nanak, through the Guru one recognises the Naam. ॥4॥
665.3: Raag Dhanasari, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). Fools and the ignorant amass flimsy (perishable) wealth; the manmukhs, blind and ignorant, have gone astray. From the wealth of poisonous Maya there is ever pain; it does not go along (at the end), nor is anything gained (by it). One obtains the true wealth through the Guru's teaching; flimsy wealth comes and goes again and again. Astray, the ignorant manmukhs all die; they drown in the world-ocean, (reaching) neither this shore nor the far shore. (Those whom) the True Guru meets, by perfect fortune, stay dyed in the True One, day and night, in bairag. In all four ages the true Bani is Amrit; by perfect fortune (through it one) merges in the Lord's Name. The Siddhas and seekers, all in the world, long (for it); (but) it is attained by perfect fortune alone. Everything is the True One; he himself is true; rare is the one who recognises that sublime Brahm (the Supreme Lord). The True One, ever true, himself makes the Truth firm (in the heart); O Nanak, (God) himself watches over (all), and himself attaches (them) to the Truth. ॥4॥
Bairag: in Gurbani often a loving longing for the Lord, not only renunciation of the world.

The four ages: Satjug, Treta, Duapar and Kalyug of the Puranic count; that is, at all times. The Siddhas are yogis held to have reached perfection; the seekers (sadhiks), those who practise the disciplines of yoga.
666.1: Raag Dhanasari, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). The worth and measure of the Name cannot be told; blessed are those people who attune their love to the Name of the One. True is the Guru's teaching, (and through it comes) reflection on the True One; (God) himself forgives, and grants (this) reflection. Wondrous is the Lord's Name; God himself makes it heard; in this age of Kalyug, one obtains it through the Guru. We are fools, utter fools in our minds; (we) do all our deeds in Haumai. By the Guru's grace Haumai departs; (God) himself forgives and unites (one with himself). The wealth of poisonous Maya (breeds) great pride; in pride one drowns, and receives no honour. When self-conceit is given up, there is peace for ever; through the Guru's teaching I praise that True One. That Creator himself fashions (the creation); apart from him there is no other at all. Only the one whom he attaches to the Truth is attached to it; O Nanak, through the Naam there is peace for ever, hereafter (too). ॥4॥
666.2: Raag Dhanasari, Ghar 4, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. We are beggars, mendicants (at your door); you are your own Master, the Giver. Be merciful and grant the Name to (me,) your begging servant, that I may stay ever dyed in (your) love. I am a sacrifice to your True Name. You alone are the root of creation, (the Maker) of all; there is no other, no second. Many rounds (of birth) have fallen to (me,) the miser; now show (me) some mercy. Be merciful and grant (me) the sight of yourself; bestow such a gift. Says Nanak: the curtains of doubt have opened, and by the Guru's grace (God) is known; a true love has taken hold within, and the mind has come to trust the True Guru. ॥3॥
666.3: Raag Dhanasari, Ghar 1, Chaupade, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. The Sants and devotees who serve the Lord: (the Lord) takes away all their sins. Show mercy to us (too), O Master; keep (us) in the Sangat that is dear to you. I cannot tell the Lord's virtues, O Banwari. We sinners are stones sinking in water; in your mercy carry us stones across. The poisonous rust that has clung through birth after birth is scoured away by clinging to the Saadh Sangat (the company of the holy), as gold heated in the fire has its dross cut away and removed. Day and night I repeat the Lord, Har Har; repeating (him), I keep the Lord, Har Har Har, in my heart. The Lord, Har Har Har, is the perfect medicine in the world; repeating the Lord, Har Har, Haumai is slain. O Lord, Har Har, inaccessible, unfathomable to understanding, beyond the farthest, O infinite Being, show mercy to your servant, O Life of the world, and uphold the honour of servant Nanak. ॥4॥
Banwari (wearer of the garland of forest flowers, a name of Krishna): in Gurbani, a name of God.
667.1: Raag Dhanasari, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). The Lord's Sants who have repeated (the Name of) the Lord: their pain, doubt and fear have fled. (God) himself has had them do his service, and the Guru's teaching has awakened within them. One imbued with the Lord's Name is a bairagi, detached (from Maya). He has heard the telling of the Lord, Har Har, and it pleases his mind; through the Guru's teaching his love is fixed on the Lord. O Lord and Master, (you are) the caste of your Sants; you are the Master, we are players in your show. Whatever understanding you give, O Lord and Master, such words do we speak. What are we? Little worms, tiny insects; you are the great Being, the greatest of all. We cannot tell your state or your extent, O God; how can we, the unfortunate, meet you? O Lord God, my Master, show mercy, that we may be joined to the service of the Lord, Har Har. Make Nanak the servant of your servants, O God, that we may keep telling of the Lord. ॥4॥
667.2: Raag Dhanasari, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). The Lord's Sant is the True Guru, the true Being, who speaks the Bani of the Lord, Har Har. Whoever speaks it or hears it is set free; I am ever a sacrifice to him (the Guru). O Sants of the Lord, listen with your ears to (his) praise. Listen to the telling of the Lord, Har Har, even for an instant, a moment, and all sins and misdeeds are washed away. Those who have found such a Sant, the Saadh (the Guru), are great, the greatest of beings. O God, my Master, we beg for the dust of their feet; O Lord, a deep longing (for it) has taken hold of us. O God, my Master, the Lord, Har Har, is a tree that bears fruit; those who have repeated (his Name) are satisfied. Drinking the Amrit of the Lord, Har Har, they are fulfilled; all their hunger is gone. Those whose fortune is great, lofty and high, have repeated the Lord's Name. O Lord God, my Master, unite (me) with their company; servant Nanak is the slave of their slaves. ॥4॥
667.3: Raag Dhanasari, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). We are blind, utterly blind, steeped in the poison of the senses' objects; how can we walk in the Guru's way? May the True Guru, the Giver of peace, show kindness and attach us to the hem of his robe. O Gursikh friends, walk in the Guru's way. Whatever the Guru says, take that as good; the telling of the Lord, Har Har, is unlike any other. Listen, O Sants of the Lord, O brothers: serve the Guru, quickly, without delay. Serving the True Guru, tie up the Lord('s Name) as provisions for the journey; do not reckon on today or tomorrow. O Sants of the Lord, repeat the Lord's Name; the Lord's Sant walks with the Lord (in step with his will). Those who have repeated the Lord have become the very form of the Lord; the Lord, the Player of wondrous plays, has met them. I long to repeat the Lord, Har Har; O Lord, O Banwali, show mercy. O Lord, unite servant Nanak with the Saadh Sangat; may we be the dust of the feet of the holy. ॥4॥
668.1: Raag Dhanasari, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). The Lord, Har Har, the Lord and Master, has become the raindrop (for me); I am the chatrik (rain-bird), crying out and crying out. O Lord God, Har Har, show your mercy; O Lord, put (that drop) in my mouth, even for an instant. Without the Lord I cannot live even for a moment. As the addict dies without his drug, so without the Lord I die. You, O Lord, are a pool beyond all depth; we cannot find even a trace of your limit. You are beyond, beyond, beyond the farthest, O Master; you alone know your own state and extent. The Lord's Sants who have repeated (the Name of) the Lord are dyed in the Guru's deep crimson (love). Devotion to the Lord, Har Har, has taken shape (in them), and great is their glory; repeating the Lord, they have won the highest honour. He himself is the Master, he himself the servant; he himself makes the way (of devotion). Servant Nanak is in your refuge; O Lord, keep the honour of your devotees. ॥4॥
668.2: Raag Dhanasari, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). Tell (me), O brother, the dharma of Kalyug: how may we, who long to be free, be set free? Repeating the Lord, Har Har, is the boat, the Lord is the raft; one who has repeated the Lord swims and crosses over. O dear Lord, keep the honour of your servant. Have (me) repeat your own Name, Har Har; I have asked for devotion alone. Those servants of the Lord are dear to the Lord who have repeated the Lord through the (Guru's) word. The account that Chitr and Gupt had written, the whole balance owed to Jam, is cleared. The Lord's Sants have repeated the Lord, Har Har, in their minds, joining the company of the holy; the blazing sun, the fire of craving, is put out (in them), and the moon of Shiv, the auspicious One, has risen with its cool light. You are the great Being, great, inaccessible, beyond the senses; you yourself are all, by yourself. O God, be gracious to servant Nanak; make (him) a slave of your slaves' slaves. ॥4॥
Chitr and Gupt are, by tradition, the two recorders at Dharam Raj's court who write down the deeds of every being.
Shiv here means the auspicious One, the giver of good, not the god Shiva.
668.3: Raag Dhanasari, Ghar 5, Dupade, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. Enshrining (him) in the heart and dwelling on (him), one repeats Murari, Ram and Ram alone, the Name of the Enticer of the mind, (in whom) the perfect Guru has revealed the Master, unseen, beyond the senses, beyond the farthest. The Lord (Ram) is the paaras and the sandalwood; we are wood and iron. When (we) came into the true company (Satsang) of the Lord, of Hari, the Lord made (us) gold and sandalwood. (Some) recite the nine (grammars) and the six (Shastras) by heart; my Lord God is not pleased this way. Says servant Nanak: meditate on the Lord in the heart always; in this way my Lord God is pleased. ॥2॥
Paaras: the philosopher's stone, held to turn iron into gold at a touch; sandalwood is held to make the trees near it fragrant. Murari (the foe of the demon Mur): a name of God.
The nine and the six: by the Darpan and the Shabdarth, the nine Sanskrit grammars and the six Shastras (schools of philosophy).
668.4: Raag Dhanasari, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). Speak (his) virtues, seek the Lord, serve the True Guru: meditate in this way on the Name of the Lord, Har Har. You will be pleasing in the Lord's court, you will not come into birth again, you will merge in the Light of the Lord, Har Har Har. O mind, repeat the Lord's Name, and you will be at peace in every way. The Lord's praise is lofty, above all else; serve the Lord, Har Har Har, and (that service) sets you free. When the Lord, the treasure of mercy, showed (mercy), the Guru gave the Lord's devotion; then love for the Lord came about. Many cares are forgotten, the Lord's Name is enshrined in the heart; O Nanak, the Lord has become the companion. ॥2॥
669.1: Raag Dhanasari, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). Read the Lord, write the Lord, repeat the Lord, sing the Lord: the Lord carries (you) across the terrifying world-ocean. In mind, in word and in heart meditate on the Lord, and, content, utter in this way the Name of the Lord, Murari. In the mind one should repeat (the Name of) the Lord, the Master of the world, joining the company of the Saadh (the Guru), O friend. Bliss abides always, day and night, (if you) sing the praise of the Lord, Banwari. When the Lord, Har Har, cast his glance (of grace), then the urge arose in the mind; (we) repeated the Name of the Lord, Har Har, and our liberation came about. Keep the honour of servant Nanak, O my Master; O Lord, he has come and fallen at your refuge. ॥2॥
669.2: Raag Dhanasari, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). The eighty-four Siddhas, the Buddhas, the thirty-three crore (gods) and the silent sages, all of them long for your Name, O dear Lord. By the Guru's grace some rare one obtains it: those on whose foreheads love (for the Name) was written from the very start. O mind, repeat the Name of Ram alone; the Lord's praise is the most exalted deed. Those who sing and hear your praise, O Master: to them I am ever a sacrifice. O Lord and Master, Cherisher of those who come to your refuge, what you give, that alone do I receive. O merciful to the meek, in your mercy grant (it): Nanak longs for the Lord's Simran (remembrance). ॥2॥
The Buddhas: the enlightened, like Gautam Buddha; the thirty-three crore: the gods as tradition counts them.
669.3: Raag Dhanasari, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). Servants and Sikhs all come (to the Guru's door) to worship, and all sing the sublime Bani of the Lord, Har Har; (but) the Lord accepts the singing and hearing of those who have accepted the True Guru's command as true, wholly true. O brothers, utter the praises of the Lord; the Lord is the tirath, the crossing over the world-ocean. At the Lord's door those are held in high regard, O Sants, who have come to know the telling of the Lord. He himself is the Guru, and he himself the disciple; the Lord God himself is the doer of wondrous plays. O servant Nanak, he alone will meet the Lord whom (the Lord) himself unites; leave all else: that (praise) alone pleases the Lord. ॥2॥
669.4: Raag Dhanasari, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). The Lord fulfils desires and gives every peace; the Kamdhenu (the cow that grants every wish) is in his power. On such a Lord one should meditate, O my soul; then you will find every peace, O my mind. O mind, repeat Sat Naam, the True Name; ever (repeat) Sat Naam. Here and hereafter the face shines bright, (if) one meditates daily on the Lord, the all-pervading Being, the Immaculate. Where the Lord's Simran has come about, every trouble has gone from there; by great fortune is the Lord repeated. The Guru has given servant Nanak this understanding: by repeating the Lord, the world-ocean is crossed. ॥2॥
670.1: Raag Dhanasari, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). O my King, may the joy of seeing the Lord be mine. My pain you know, O King; what could anyone else know of it? You are the True Master, the eternal One, O my King; whatever you do is all true. Whom can one call false, O King? There is no second at all. You are at work in all, O King; day and night, all meditate on you. From you alone do all beg, O my King; you alone bestow gifts on all. Everyone is within you, O my King; there is none outside you. Every being is yours, you are everyone's, O my King; in you alone all are absorbed. Everyone's hope is you, O my Beloved; on you alone all meditate, O my King. As it pleases you, so keep (me), O my Beloved; you are the True One, O Emperor of Nanak. ॥4॥
670.2: Raag Dhanasari, Ghar 1, Chaupade, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. O Destroyer of the round of births, Breaker of sorrows, O Master, Lover of devotion, O Formless One, millions of offences are wiped out in an instant when one, through the Guru, cherishes the Naam. My mind is attached to the beloved Lord (Ram). God, merciful to the meek, has shown mercy, and has brought the five enemies (lust, anger, greed, attachment and pride) under control. Lovely is your place, lovely your form; your devotees shine in your court. O Master, Giver to all beings, in your mercy save (me). Your colour is not seen, your form cannot be made out; who can reckon your power? You pervade the water, the land and the sky, every place, O Girdhari, of inaccessible form. All your servants sing your praises; you are the imperishable, all-pervading Being, O Murari. As it pleases you, so keep (me), O Master; servant Nanak is in your refuge, at your door. ॥4॥
Girdhari: the upholder of the mountain, a name of Krishna; here the one Lord.
670.3: Raag Dhanasari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Without water the fish gives up its life, for it has grown to love the water; for love of the lotus the bumblebee perishes, for it finds no way to get out. Now, O mind, love has been formed with the One alone, who neither dies nor departs, and is ever with (us); (he) is recognised through the True Guru's Shabad. For lust the elephant is caught and trapped; the poor creature falls into another's power; for love of a sound the deer gives up its head; for that very love it is slain. Seeing his family, the mortal is lured by greed and clings to Maya; he is utterly absorbed (in it) and has made it his own, (yet) he must surely leave it and go. One who loves any other than Gobind: know that he is ever miserable. Says Nanak: the Guru has made (me) understand this: in the love of God there is joy forever. ॥4॥
The elephant is said to be caught by a paper she-elephant set over a covered pit; the deer, spellbound by the hunter's bell (ghanda hera), is killed.
671.1: Raag Dhanasari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). In his grace (the Lord) has given me the Naam, and set (me) free from (my) bonds; all worldly entanglement has slipped from (my) mind; (he) has joined (me) to the Guru's feet. In the Saadh Sangat I have let go of the anxious hope placed in others; the proud intellect, attachment and the mind's cravings I have buried in a pit I dug. No one remains my enemy, nor am I the enemy of anyone; God (Brahm) has spread out this expanse, (and is) within (all); this understanding I have gained from the True Guru. I have made every one my own friend, and I am a friend to all. The separation in (my) mind has fled far away; then my King united (me with himself). Stubbornness has perished, the Amrit has come to dwell (within), and the Guru's Shabad tastes sweet. Nanak has seen the all-pervading Lord (Ramaiya) dwelling in all, in water, land and sky. ॥4॥
671.2: Raag Dhanasari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Since I met with the sight of the Saadh (the Guru), those blessed days have come (in which,) singing Kirtan, there is ever great bliss, and (I) have found the all-pervading Creator. Now I have sung the praise of Ram in my mind; light has dawned, there is lasting peace in (my) mind: (I) have found the Perfect True Guru. The Treasure of virtues has come to dwell within (my) heart, and so pain, doubt and fear have fled; the thing beyond the reach of the senses has been obtained, and (my) love is fixed on Ram's Name. Anxiety has turned to freedom from anxiety, brooding to freedom from brooding; sorrow, greed and attachment are spent. By (his) grace the ills of Haumai are erased, and (we) have become fearless of Jam. Attending on the Guru, serving the Guru, the Guru's command: (these) are pleasing (to me). Says Nanak, I am a sacrifice to the Guru who has pulled (us) out from Jam. ॥4॥
671.3: Raag Dhanasari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). He to whom body, mind and wealth belong, everything is his; he alone is skilful and wise. He alone has heard my pain and my joy, and then my state has turned good. What the soul asks is heeded by the One alone; (people) have worn themselves out making many other efforts, (but) their worth is not reckoned even as a sesame seed's. The Naam, the Amrit, the priceless diamond: the Guru has given (it to me) as a mantra; it does not fall away, nor waver; it has settled firm, and (I), made whole, am content. Those (divides) of me and you that stood somewhat between (us): even the talk of them has vanished. Ornaments, melted together, have become one lump, and so it is spoken of as gold. The Light has shone forth; there are Sahaj, peace and glory; the unstruck (Anhad) Bani sounds (within). Says Nanak, (I) have built an unshakeable home; the Guru has made (its) arrangement. ॥4॥
672.1: Raag Dhanasari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). The greatest of kings and the lords of the land: their thirst has not been quenched; drunk with Maya's pleasures, they cling (to it); (their) eyes see nothing (else). In the poison of Maya no one has ever found contentment. As fire is never sated by fuel, how can (one) be content without the Lord? Day after day one eats meals of many dishes, yet his hunger is not ended; he strives like a dog, and searches through all four quarters. The lustful lecher may have many women, yet his eyeing of others' homes does not stop; day after day he does (wrong), does it again, and repents; in grief and greed he withers away. The Name of the Lord, Har Har, is boundless and priceless, the one treasure of Amrit. Peace, Sahaj and bliss dwell in (the hearts of) the Sants; O Nanak, (this) is known through the Guru. ॥4॥
672.2: Raag Dhanasari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Nothing that this (mortal) runs after again and again can come near (this Amrit); the one to whom the Guru has given this Amrit, it graces him alone. The one who has come to taste the One relish has no hunger for food and drink, or any other, dwelling in his mind. The mind of the one who has received a single drop (of it) has blossomed, and (his) body has turned green; I cannot describe his praise; his worth cannot be told. It was not won by toil, nor by service; it came and was found, unlooked for. The one on whom my Master showed mercy has practised the Guru's teaching. (He is) merciful to the meek, ever kind, the sustainer of all beings; like warp and weft, Gopal is blended with Nanak, as a mother with her child. ॥4॥
672.3: Raag Dhanasari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). I am a sacrifice to my own Guru, who has made the Name of the Lord, Har Har, firm within (me); who, in the great wilderness and the darkness, has shown (me) the straight path. Gopal, Gobind, is our breath of life, who, here and hereafter, takes thought for all our needs. By remembering him come all treasures, honour, greatness and full respect; taking his Name, millions of sins are destroyed; the devotees, every one, long for the dust (of his feet). If anyone wants all his heart's wishes, he should serve the One, the Treasure. Remembering the Supreme Lord, the infinite Master, one crosses over. (I) have found coolness, calm and great peace; in the company of the Sants (my) honour has been kept covered. Gathering the Lord's wealth, the Lord's Name as food: this Nanak has made his delicacy. ॥4॥
673.1: Raag Dhanasari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). The deeds that will put you to shame, that very way you have practised: slandering the Sant and honouring the Saakat; such a perverse way you have held fast. Lost in attachment to Maya, you have strayed into love of another. The city of Harichand, the green leaves of the forest: such, O brother, is your worth. Sandal paste is smeared on the body, (yet) the donkey's pleasure is in the company of ashes; (so) you have no taste for the Amrit; (your) love is for the swindler's drug of the senses' pleasures. The noble Sants are met by good fortune; in this world (they) are pure and holy. The treasure of (your) birth is going in vain, won away in exchange for glass. The sins and sorrows of birth after birth fled, (when) the Guru put the collyrium of wisdom in (the) eyes; in the Saadh Sangat (a person) has come out of these sorrows; O Nanak, (there is now) love for the One. ॥4॥
Saakat (Sanskrit shakta): a worshipper of Shakti (Maya); in Gurbani, one cut off from God and lost in Maya.
The city of Harichand (Harichandauri): a city seen in the sky, a mirage that vanishes as one draws near.
673.2: Raag Dhanasari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Before the Sants may I carry water, wave the fan and grind (the corn), and sing the praise of Govind's virtues; with every breath may (my) mind remember the Naam, and may (I) find this treasure of rest. O my Sain (Lord), show (me) mercy; give me such understanding, my Master, that I may meditate on you for ever and ever. By your grace may attachment and pride let go of (me), and (my) wandering be destroyed; the One whose form is bliss pervades all; wherever I go and look, (he is there). You are kind and merciful, a treasure of grace, O Gosain (Lord of the world), purifier of the fallen; millions of joys, bliss and kingdoms are gained when, even for an instant, I speak (your Name) aloud. Only that chanting, austerity and devotion is complete which is pleasing to God's mind. Repeating the Naam, all thirst is quenched; Nanak is sated and fulfilled. ॥4॥
673.3: Raag Dhanasari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). She (Maya) who has brought under her sway the worlds of the three qualities, the world of the four quarters, and has shattered sacrifices, holy baths, austerities and sacred places: what (can) this poor creature (do)? When (I) took hold of God's shelter, then (I) was set free; by the grace of the Saadh (the Guru), (I) sang of the Lord, Har Har Har, and then the sickness of the senses' pleasures ended. She cannot be heard, no mouth of hers speaks, and as she bewitches she is never seen; (yet) she slips in such a swindler's drug and leads (all) astray that she seems sweet to every mind. Mother, father, son, friend, brother: in every home she has mixed in division; with one there is more, with another less; all fight and fight to death. I am a sacrifice to my own True Guru, who has let (me) see this play: the world burns in a hidden fire, (but) Maya does not take hold of the devotees. By the Sant's grace (I) have found great peace, and all bonds are cut; Nanak has found the Name of the Lord, Har Har, as (his) wealth, and, having earned it, has brought it to his own home. ॥5॥
673.4: Raag Dhanasari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). You are the Giver, the Master, the Sustainer, our Leader and our Lord; every instant you alone sustain (us); we children live by your support. With (but) one tongue, which of (your) virtues can be told? O countless, endless Lord, no one has found your end. You destroy our millions of wrongs, and instruct (us) in many ways; we are ignorant, of small and meagre understanding; you keep to your own age-old way. (We are) in your refuge, (our) hope is in you; you alone are (our) friend, the giver of comfort. Protect (us), O merciful Protector; says Nanak, (we are) the slaves of your house. ॥3॥
674.1: Raag Dhanasari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Worship, fasts, tilak marks, ritual baths, much giving of alms and charity: by none of these disciplines is the Master won, (though people) speak sweet words. Repeating the Name of God, the mind is at rest; all search for him in many ways, (but he is) hard (to reach), and cannot be won. Chanting, austerities, wandering over the earth, austerities done upside down, taking (the breath) up into the sky (the tenth door): by these ways the Master is not won over, (nor) by the practice of Yoga, (nor by that of) the Jains. The Naam, the Amrit, the priceless praise of the Lord: he alone has obtained it on whom (God's) grace rests. Those servants who in the Saadh Sangat have met God in love, O Nanak, pass the night (of life) in peace. ॥3॥
674.2: Raag Dhanasari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). (One who) frees (me) from bonds, unites (me) with God and recites (to me) the Name of the Lord, Har Har, (who) makes this mind steady and still, so that it never runs anywhere again: is there any such friend of mine? (To him) I would give all my goods, my life and my heart; I would offer up my consciousness. Others' wealth, others' bodies, slander of others: may (my) love not cling to these; (may I have) the company of the Sants and converse with the Sants, (and may my) mind stay awake in the Lord's Kirtan. O Treasure of virtues, merciful, all-pervading God, O kind (giver) of all comforts, Nanak begs the gift of your Name, O Gopal, as a child (asks) of its mother. ॥3॥
674.3: Raag Dhanasari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). The Lord, Har Har, has saved (his) Sants; whoever wishes harm to the Lord's servant, him in turn (the Lord) strikes down. (The Lord) himself has become the helper of his servant; the slanderers have fled, defeated; wandering and wandering, they died there, (and) never again (came) into (their) home. Nanak has fallen into the refuge of the Destroyer of pain, and ever sings the praises of the Infinite One; the slanderer's face has been blackened in the court of both the next world and this. ॥2॥
674.4: Raag Dhanasari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Now (I) have called to mind the Lord, the Protector; (he) has made the fallen pure in an instant, and destroyed all disease. In the company of the Saadh (the Guru) the meeting came about, and lust, anger and greed were slain; remembering the perfect Narayan again and again, (I) have carried all (my) companions across. O mind, the One (God's Name) is the root of all medicines and mantras; (I) have set (my) faith in God within (my) mind. Nanak ever longs for the dust of (his) feet, and is a sacrifice (to him) again and again. ॥2॥
675.1: Raag Dhanasari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). My love has become fixed on Ram. My True Guru is ever my helper, who has cut down the very banner (Ketu) of pain. Giving (his) hand, (he) has saved (me), and, making (me) his own, wiped out all (my) pain; (he) has blackened the faces of the slanderers; he himself is the helper of his servant. The True Master has become (their) protector; he has saved (them), clasping (them) to his bosom; O Nanak, singing the Lord's praises, (they) have become fearless, and ever enjoy peace. ॥2॥
Ketu: a banner; it is also the name of an ill-omened planet of astrology.
675.2: Raag Dhanasari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Your Name, O Merciful One, is the medicine. I, the afflicted, have not known your state; (still) you yourself cherish (me). Show grace, my Master, and take away the love of another; cut (our) bonds and make (us) your own, so that (we) may never come back defeated. Having fallen into your refuge, I live; you are the all-powerful, all-pervading, merciful (Lord). At all hours may I worship God; Nanak is ever a sacrifice (to him). ॥2॥
675.3: Raag Dhanasari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. Alas, alas! O God, save (us). Nothing at all can be done by us, my Lord; in your mercy, grant (us) your Name. The world is an ocean ablaze with the fire of (attachment to) family; (over it) lies the darkness of doubt, attachment and ignorance. (The soul is) now high, now low, now in pleasure, now in pain; (yet it is) never sated: craving and hunger (cling to it). Raising up desires in the mind, (it takes on) the sickness of sensual vice; the five enemies (lust, anger, greed, attachment and pride), wholly beyond taming, keep company with it. (O God,) the beings, the world, the breath of life and wealth are (all) yours. O Nanak, know the Lord to be ever near. ॥4॥
675.4: Raag Dhanasari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Driving away the pain of the poor, the Master himself keeps (the honour) of his servant. The Lord is the boat that carries (us) across (the world-ocean), the treasure (of all comforts); no sorrow can touch (his servant). In the company of the Saadh (the Guru), worship Gopal. I can see no other discipline; by this effort pass through the age of Kalyug. From the beginning to the end the merciful One fills all; there is none but him. Repeating (the Name of) the Lord, put an end to (your) birth and death; remember that Master alone. Each Veda, Simriti and Shastra tells (of him), and the devotees reflect (on him); in the Saadh Sangat liberation is found, and the darkness (of ignorance) is destroyed. His servant's support is the lotus feet (of the Lord), (his) one wealth and capital. God is Nanak's support: (his) strength, (his) honour and (his) true refuge. ॥4॥
676.1: Raag Dhanasari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Searching and searching, I met the holy one (the Guru), and the perfect Guru made (me) understand that all other ways are of no use; (so) I have meditated on the Name of the Lord, Har Har. Therefore I have taken the shelter of Gopal; I have sought the refuge of the perfect Supreme God, and all (my) entanglements are gone. Heaven, the mortal world, the underworld and all the spheres of the earth are gripped by Maya. Meditate on the Name of the Lord, Har Har, which saves the soul and carries all (its) lineage across. O Nanak, as the Name of the stainless Lord (Niranjan) is sung, all treasures are found; (but) only a rare one, to whom the Master in his mercy gives (this gift), has known (it). ॥3॥
676.2: Raag Dhanasari, Ghar 2, Chaupade, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. (Those caught in Maya) busy themselves with straw, (with things) they leave behind when they go; (they cling to) entanglements that are of no use (to them); they love those who will not go along with them, and those who are enemies they take for friends. In such doubt the world has gone astray; the fool is losing the precious gift of human birth. Truth and dharma he cannot bear even to look upon; taking falsehood and fraud for sweet, he is wrapped up in them. He loves the gift and has forgotten the Giver; the poor wretch has no thought of death. He rises up and weeps for what belongs to another, and squanders all his duty and dharma. He does not understand the Hukam (God's will), (so his) comings and goings (in birth and death go on); he commits sins, and then (comes) remorse. (O God,) whatever pleases you is accepted; I am a sacrifice to your will. Humble Nanak is your bondsman, your servant; God, my Master, keeps (him) safe. ॥4॥
676.3: Raag Dhanasari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). For me, the meek, God's Name is the support; for earning, (my) livelihood is (the Name of) the Lord, Har Har; for storing up, (I have) the Lord's Name alone; (for whoever gathers it,) it is of use to him in this world and the next. Imbued with the Naam, in the love of the infinite God, the holy sing the virtues of the One, the Formless Lord. The glory of the holy one is deep humility; the Sant has known the Lord's praise to be (his) greatness. In the hearts of the Sants, devotion to Govind is bliss; in the hearts of the Sants is peace; (their) anxiety is gone. Wherever the holy and the Sants gather, there they sing the Lord's praise with music and verse. In the gathering of the holy there is bliss and rest; (but) he alone gains their company on whose forehead (the writ of) grace is written. Joining both hands I pray that, washing (the Sants') feet, I may speak (of the Lord), the treasure of virtues. God, merciful and kind, is ever present (to the Sants); Nanak lives by the dust of the Sants' feet. ॥4॥
677.1: Raag Dhanasari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Why should he fear who cherishes the Master (in his heart)? Fearing and fearing, the wretched manmukhs waste away. (He) over whose head stands the Gurdev (the divine Guru), as mother and father, whose form bears fruit and whose service is pure; he whose capital is the One, the stainless Lord, on joining the Saadh Sangat, light dawns (within him). The Giver of all beings fills every place; through the Lord's Name millions of troubles are erased. All the pain of birth and death is destroyed (for him) in whose mind and body (the Lord) comes to dwell, through the Guru. The one whom (the Lord) himself attaches to the hem of his robe alone finds a place in the Lord's court. They alone are devotees who have pleased the True One; they have been freed from the sway of Jamkaal (death). True is the Master, true (his) court; who can reflect and tell (his) worth? Dwelling within every heart, he upholds all; Nanak begs for the dust of the Sants' feet. ॥4॥
677.2: Raag Dhanasari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. (O God,) at home and abroad (your servant) trusts in you; you are with your servant. Be merciful, O my own beloved God, that I may repeat the Name in the Lord's love. The servant's strength is his own God. Whatever you do and cause to be done, my Lord, that counsel is accepted (by him). (His) honour is the Supreme God, (his) liberation Narayan, (his) wealth the accounts of the virtues of Gopal. O Nanak, the servants of the Lord, Har Har, (abide) in the refuge of his feet; the Sants have known this to be the way. ॥2॥
Narayan: a name of Vishnu (he whose dwelling is the waters); in Gurbani the one Lord.
677.3: Raag Dhanasari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). (They) have received all their heart's wishes from God; the Guru has held (them) to his breast and saved (them). (The Guru) has not let them burn in the world-ocean; not one (of them) has called it hard to cross. Those in whose minds is true faith, beholding again and again the glory of the Master, are ever in bliss and delight. In the refuge of the feet of the perfect Supreme God, (they) have seen the Knower of hearts face to face. O Nanak, knowing and understanding (them), (the Lord) has made (them) his own and kept safe the tender shoot of his devotees. ॥2॥
677.4: Raag Dhanasari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Wherever I look, there (God) is present; he is far from no place. He pervades everything; O mind, I meditate on him for ever. He who does not part (from us) here or hereafter should be counted (our) companion; the pleasure that perishes in an instant should be called a petty pleasure. He cherishes (all), giving them nourishment, and nothing (of what he gives) falls short; with every breath he takes care (of all): he is my God. God, who cannot be deceived or pierced, who is infinite, whose form is lofty, wondrous and beyond compare: repeating (his Name) over and over, his servants delight in bliss. Give (me) that understanding, merciful God, by which I may worship you. Nanak begs a gift of you, God: the dust of the holy ones' feet. ॥4॥
678.1: Raag Dhanasari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). He who sent you has called you back; come home in peace and Sahaj. In bliss and joy, in the strain of Sahaj, sing (the Lord's) virtues, and rule an unshakable kingdom. Come home, my friend. The Lord himself has driven off your enemies, and the calamity is past. God, the Doer of all, has brought (you) to light before all, and (your) fleeing and running are over. In the home the music of rejoicing plays day after day; your own Master has honoured you. Stay steady, and never waver, upheld by the Guru's word; acclaim rings across the whole earth, and (your) face is bright in the court (of the Lord). He whose beings they are has himself turned them back; he himself has become (their) helper. The Doer has worked a wonder; O Nanak, true for ever is (his) greatness. ॥4॥
678.2: Raag Dhanasari, Ghar 6, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. Hear my prayer, beloved Sants: without the Lord no one is liberated. O mind, do pure deeds; the Lord is the boat that carries (you) across; other entanglements will be of no use to you at all. Service of the radiant Supreme Lord (Paarbrahm) is (true) life: this teaching the Guru has given me. One should not set (one's) love on what has no worth at all; at the very end it does not go along. O holy one, beloved of the Lord, worship (the Lord) in your mind and body; in his company your bonds are loosed. Hold fast to the refuge of the Supreme Lord, (keep his) lotus feet in your heart; one should make no screen of hope in any other. He alone is the devotee, the man of wisdom, of meditation and of austerity, O Nanak, on whom (the Lord) bestows his grace. ॥3॥
678.3: Raag Dhanasari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). My dear one, it is good, O brother, it is good, so good, to beg for the Lord. Open your eyes and see, hear the words of the Saadh (the Guru), keep the Lord of life in your mind: all must die. Sandal and perfume, the many tastes and pleasures you enjoy, these vices of Maya: see, they are all insipid; the Name of Gobind alone is good, say the holy. You have taken body and wealth for your own, and have not repeated the Lord's Name even for an instant; see, nothing of riches and wealth will go with you. He whose fortune, O brother, is good has taken shelter, holding to the hem of the Sant; those in the company of the Saadh, O brother, are not tormented by Jam. He has found, O brother, the supreme treasure, and (his) pride is gone; O Nanak, (his) mind is fixed on the One, the Formless Lord. ॥2॥
679.1: Raag Dhanasari, Ghar 7, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. Remember the One Lord, remember the One, remember the One, my beloved. He carries (you) across the vast and terrifying world-ocean of strife and suffering, greed and attachment. (The one who) keeps him in mind with every breath, every instant, day and night, (who), repeating (the Name) in the Saadh Sangat without a qualm, holds (its) treasure in the mind, (who) bows to the lotus feet (of the Lord) and reflects on the virtues of Gobind: O Nanak, the dust of the holy ones' feet brings (him) joy and peace. ॥2॥
679.2: Raag Dhanasari, Ghar 8, Dupade, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. I remember (God); remembering him again and again I find peace, and with every breath I cherish (him). In this world and the world beyond he is with me as my helper; wherever (I may be), he is my protector. The Guru's word dwells with (my) soul; it does not drown in water, no thief carries it off, and no fire can burn it. (It is to me) as wealth to the penniless, a staff to the blind, and as a mother's milk to her child. In the ocean (of the world) Nanak has found the Lord as his ship; the Merciful One has shown (him) mercy. ॥2॥
Dupade (du, two; pad, stanza): hymns of two stanzas.
679.3: Raag Dhanasari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Gobind has become kind and merciful, and I water my heart with the Amrit (of the Name). The nine treasures, the riddhis and the siddhis stay at the feet of the Lord's servant. The Sants are in bliss in every place; at home and abroad, the Master of the devotees (is with them); he pervades every place. No one can come up to the one who has the Lord of the world (Gusain) at his side. The dread of Jam is erased by remembering him; Nanak meditates on (his) Name. ॥2॥
The nine treasures (nidhis): by tradition, the nine treasures of Kuber, the god of wealth; that is, all the riches of the world. Riddhis and siddhis: wealth and the miraculous powers of yoga.
679.4: Raag Dhanasari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). The man of wealth looks on his wealth and is proud; the owner of land is vain (of his land); the king believes the whole kingdom is his; just so, the Lord's servant leans on the Master. If anyone keeps his own support (in mind), (that support) acts for him to the full measure of its means, and does not hold back its strength. (The Lord's servants) have given up all others and rest on the One alone; crying, refuge, refuge, they have come (to his door). By the Sants' grace (their) minds have become pure; O Nanak, they have sung the Lord's praises. ॥2॥
679.5: Raag Dhanasari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). One who has taken on the colour of the Lord's love in this age is the one called a hero. He conquers his own self, and all things come under his sway, whose True Guru is the Perfect One. Let us sing of the Master with the love of the soul: taking his refuge, meditating on the Naam, and merging with him in Sahaj. May the feet of (your) servants dwell in my heart, and in their company may my body be made pure. O treasure of mercy, give (me) the dust of (your) servant's feet; for Nanak this alone is peace. ॥2॥
680.1: Raag Dhanasari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). (A man) contrives and deceives people, but the Knower of hearts knows (all). He sins, and having sinned denies it, and puts on the garb of those free of desire. He thinks you far away, O God, (yet you are) near. The greedy one looks this way, and from there looks that way, and stays caught in the round (of greed). As long as the mind's wandering is not broken, no one is free. Says Nanak: the one to whom the Master is merciful, he alone is a Sant, a devotee, a servant (of the Lord). ॥2॥
680.2: Raag Dhanasari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). His own Guru has given the Naam to the one on whose forehead (good) fortune is written. He makes (others) hold fast to the Naam and has them repeat the Naam; this is his dharma in the world. For the (Lord's) servant the Naam is greatness and renown; the Naam alone is the servant's liberation, the Naam alone his honour; whatever is to be, he accepts (as God's will). The servant who holds the wealth of the Naam in his keeping is the banker who lacks nothing. O Nanak, his dealing is in the Naam, the Naam is his mainstay, and the Naam is the profit he receives. ॥2॥
680.3: Raag Dhanasari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). (My) eyes have become pure, beholding the sight (of you); may the dust (of your feet) fall on my forehead. May I sing the Master's praises with ever deeper delight; dwell in my heart, O Gopal. You indeed are the Protector, O Merciful One. O beautiful, wise and boundless Father God, be gracious (to me), O God. (You are) the very form of supreme bliss and joy; your words are matchless and full of sweetness. With (the Lord's) feet in his heart, Nanak has tied the True Guru's Shabad securely in the fold of his garment. ॥2॥
680.4: Raag Dhanasari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). In his own way he feeds (us), in his own way he lets (us) play; he gives every comfort, enjoyment and delight, and is present within the mind itself. Our Father, Gopal, is merciful; as a mother keeps her child, so does God cherish (us). (O Lord,) you are friend and companion, the Master of every virtue; O Divine One, you abide for ever. Here and there, wherever (I look), there you alone are; may Nanak be granted the service of the Sants. ॥2॥
680.5: Raag Dhanasari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). The Sants of Damodar are kind and merciful; they burn up the poison of lust and anger. Kingship, wealth, youth, body and life: all these I have offered up as a sacrifice to them. (Those) who love the Name of the Lord in mind and body are carried across the world-ocean, with peace, Sahaj, bliss and joy. Blessed is that place, blessed are those dwellings, where the Sants make their home. Fulfil servant Nanak's heartfelt wish, O Master: may he bow before your devotees. ॥2॥
Damodar (he whose waist was bound with a cord: the child Krishna) is a name of Vishnu and Krishna in the Puranas; in Gurbani it is a name of the one God.
681.1: Raag Dhanasari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). (The perfect True Guru) has freed (me) from the mighty one (Maya), drawing me to his feet; he has given (my) mind the mantra of the Name of the One, which neither perishes nor goes anywhere. The perfect True Guru has bestowed (this) gift: he has given (me) the Name of the Lord, Har Har, for Kirtan, and I have been set free. My own God has made (them) his, and kept the honour of his devotees. Nanak has taken hold of his God's feet, and has had peace day and night. ॥2॥
681.2: Raag Dhanasari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Seizing what is others', greed, falsehood and slander: doing just these, (the Saakat) passes (his life). He holds sweet a false hope, a mirage (the deer's thirst); this is the prop he has set up for his mind. The Saakat's life passes in vain, as a mouse gnaws through loads of paper and wastes them, and they are of no use to the fool. Have mercy, O Supreme Lord, O Master, and free (me) from these bonds. Says Nanak: O God, you pull out the blind who are drowning, (bringing them) into the company of the holy. ॥2॥
Mrig trishna (the deer's thirst): the mirage of water on hot sand, which the thirsty deer runs after.
681.3: Raag Dhanasari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). As I remember God, my own Master, again and again, my body, mind and breast are cooled. Beauty, delight, peace, the wealth of my soul and my caste: the Supreme Lord is (all these) to me. (My) tongue is drunk on the Lord, the home of every essence; it is dyed in the love of its own Lord; (his) lotus feet are (my) treasure and store. The One to whom (I) belonged has himself saved (me); such is the way of the perfect God. The Giver of peace has himself united Nanak (with him); the Lord has kept (his) honour. ॥2॥
681.4: Raag Dhanasari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). (O Lord,) all the evil ones and enemies are driven off by you; your glory is plain to see. whoever troubles your devotees, you strike him down at once. I look to you always, O Lord. O Murari, be a help to (your) servant; take (him) by the hand and lift (him) out, O Friend. My Master has heard (my) prayer, and himself has done a master's part (by me). O Nanak, by repeating (the Name of) the Lord for ever and ever, bliss has come and sorrows have fled. ॥2॥
681.5: Raag Dhanasari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). (God) has spread his might in the four directions, and placed his hand on (his servant's) head. He has looked with a glance of grace, and shattered the servant's pain. The Guru, Govind, has protected the servants of the Lord; clasping (them) to his breast, the merciful, forgiving Purakh has erased all (their) failings. Whatever (his servants) ask of their own Master, that very thing he gives. O Nanak, what the (Lord's) servant says with his mouth comes true, in this world and the next. ॥2॥
682.1: Raag Dhanasari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). (God) does not let (his servant) see a hard moment; he keeps to his own age-old way (of grace). Holding out his hand, he shields his own, and cherishes (him) with every breath. My mind stays fixed on God, who is ever a help, at the beginning and at the end; blessed is our Friend. Joys have filled the mind, seeing the wondrous greatness of the Master. Remembering the Lord again and again, enjoy bliss, O Nanak; the perfect God has kept (his servant's) honour. ॥2॥
682.2: Raag Dhanasari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). One who forgets the Giver, the Master of life: count that one unfortunate. One whose mind has come to love the lotus feet (of the Lord) has found the pool of Amrit. (O Lord,) your servant has woken, in love with the Lord's Name; every trace of sloth has left his body, and (his) mind is joined to the Beloved. Wherever I look, there is Narayan; he runs like a thread through every heart. As he drinks the Naam's water, servant Nanak has let go of every other attachment. ॥2॥
682.3: Raag Dhanasari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). The tasks of the (Lord's) servant have been fulfilled; in Kalyug, amid the great poison of Maya, the Lord has kept (his) honour. As he remembers God, his own Master, again and again, Jam does not come near (him). Liberation and Baikunth are in the company of the Saadh; the servant has found the Lord's abode. The Lord's lotus feet are his servant's wealth, the resting place of millions of comforts. I remember Gobind, Damodar, day and night; Nanak is ever a sacrifice (to him). ॥2॥
Baikunth: in the Puranas, the heaven of Vishnu.
682.4: Raag Dhanasari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). I ask one gift of the Lord: that I may remember your Name, and (so) all (my) wishes be fulfilled. May your feet dwell in (my) heart, and may I find the company of the Sants; may (my) mind not be caught in the fire of grief, and may I sing (your) praises at all hours. The Lord's service, and repeating God's Name from the middle to the end (always): (this is) the state of well-being. O Nanak, (one who) is touched by love for the Supreme God is neither born nor dies again. ॥2॥
Svasti: well-being; bivastha: state. Madhyant (madhya, middle; ant, end): from the middle to the end, that is, always.
682.5: Raag Dhanasari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). I ask the Lord (alone) for all things; begging of men, one gets only toil; through remembrance of God (comes) liberation. The sages have searched the Simritis and the Puranas, and, having searched the Vedas, they proclaim: by serving the Ocean of mercy the True One is found, and both worlds become easy. All the other rites and dealings there are, without the Lord's remembrance, are empty. O Nanak, the fears of birth and death have been cut away; meeting the Saadhu (the Guru), sorrows have perished. ॥2॥
682.6: Raag Dhanasari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Craving is quenched by the Lord's Name; through the Guru's words comes great contentment, and attention is wholly fixed on God. May the great revels of Maya die out (in me); have mercy, O my Lord, merciful to the meek. Give (me) your Name, that by repeating it I may live; may (your) servant's toil be fulfilled. All wishes, kingship, comforts, delights and lasting joys (come) by singing Kirtan and repeating the Naam; O Nanak, the one in whose destiny the Creator wrote (this) from the very beginning: that servant's tasks are fulfilled. ॥2॥
683.1: Raag Dhanasari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). The Supreme Lord has taken care of his servant; the slanderers cannot stand at all; worthless, they have been blown away. Wherever I look, there is the Master; no one can come up to him. Whoever slights (his) servant is turned to ashes on the spot. The Maker has become (his) protector, he who has no end, no near shore or far. O Nanak, God has protected his servants, and struck down the slanderers and driven them out. ॥2॥
683.2: Raag Dhanasari, Ghar 9, Partal, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. O Lord, (I have come to) the refuge of (your) feet; O Gobind, destroyer of pain, give the Naam to your own servant. Cast (your) glance, O God, and in (your) grace carry (me) across; take (me) by the arm and pull (me) out of the well. (The soul) is blind with lust and anger, in the bonds of Maya; countless faults have covered and filled (its) body. Besides God there is no other protector; O Hero who shields those who come for refuge, make (me) remember the Naam. O Uplifter of the fallen, who carries all beings and creatures across: the utterance of the Vedas has not found (your) end. O Ocean of virtues and of peace, O Supreme Lord, mine of jewels: Nanak has sung of you, who love devotion. ॥2॥
Partal: a setting in which the rhythm (taal) changes again and again as the hymn is sung.
683.3: Raag Dhanasari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Remembrance is peace in this world, peace in the next, peace at all times: so the Name of Gobind should ever be taken. (By it) the sins committed long ago are wiped away; joining the Saadh Sangat, one who was dead (in spirit) comes to life. Power and youth make one forget the Lord; Maya is a great sorrow: so the great souls say. The hope and the thirst to dwell on the Lord and to sing his Kirtan: this precious gift only a fortunate one receives. O you who are able to shelter all who seek your refuge, O Indescribable One, beyond the reach of the senses: your Name is the uplifter of the fallen. O Knower of hearts, Lord and Master of Nanak: my Master fills every place. ॥2॥
683.4: Raag Dhanasari, Ghar 12, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. Salutation to the Lord, salutation! Sing the praises of Gopal, the King. One who by great fortune meets the divine Guru: by serving the Lord, (his) millions of offences are wiped out. One whose mind is dyed in (the love of God's) lotus feet: the fire of grief has no hold on that person. In the company of the Saadh (the Guru) the (world-) ocean is crossed; repeat the Name of the fearless Lord, with love. (One who remembers him) commits no fault over others' wealth, no sin, no evil deed; cruel Jam does not come near (him). God himself has put out (their) fire of craving; O Nanak, in God's refuge (beings) are saved. ॥5॥
684.1: Raag Dhanasari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Satisfaction has come to one who has eaten the food of truth (the Name), (who) has meditated on the Naam in mind, in heart and with the tongue. This is life, (remembering) the Lord is life: repeat (the Name of) the Lord in the Saadh Sangat: (this is true) life. He has (as it were) put on robes of many kinds who night and day sings the Kirtan, the praises of the Lord. He rides (as it were) on elephants, chariots and horses who beholds the Lord's path within his heart. Meditating on (God's) feet within mind and body, servant Nanak has found the Lord, the treasure of peace. ॥4॥
684.2: Raag Dhanasari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). The Guru's feet are the soul's deliverance: (the feet of the Guru) who in an instant has carried (the soul) across the vast ocean (of the world). Someone has become devoted to rituals, someone has bathed at places of pilgrimage; the Lord's servants have meditated on the Lord's Name. The Master is the cutter of bonds; servant Nanak remembers (him), the Knower of hearts. ॥2॥
684.3: Raag Dhanasari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). (O God,) may the love (for you) not break in any way: pure is the way of life of your servant. Dearer (to him) than soul, breath, mind and wealth is the Lord, who can set a dam against Haumai. May (my) love stay fixed on (God's) lotus feet: this is Nanak's prayer. ॥2॥
684.4: Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. Raag Dhanasari, by the Ninth Guru (Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji). Why, O brother, do you go to the forests to search (for God)? He dwells in all, is ever untouched (by Maya), (and) abides right with you. As fragrance dwells within the flower, as the reflection is in the mirror, so the Lord dwells within all, with no gap between; search (for him) in the heart itself, O brother. Know the One alone, outside and within: this is what the Guru's wisdom tells. O servant Nanak, until one knows oneself, doubt's moss is not cleared away. ॥2॥
684.5: Raag Dhanasari, by the Ninth Guru (Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji). O holy ones, this world has strayed, lost in doubt; it has given up the remembrance of Ram's Name and sold itself into the hands of Maya. Mother, father, brother, sons, wife: in the relish of them it stays wrapped up; in the intoxication of youth, wealth and power it stays crazed day and night. To him who is merciful to the meek, ever the destroyer of pain, its mind does not cling. O servant Nanak, among millions, only some rare one has recognised (him), becoming Gurmukh. ॥2॥
685.1: Raag Dhanasari, by the Ninth Guru (Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji). I do not hold that yogi to know the way (of yoga) in whose heart I see greed, attachment, Maya and the sense of mine. He in whom there is neither slander of others nor flattery, to whom gold and iron are alike, who stays aloof from joy and grief: call him a yogi. The fickle mind runs off in the ten directions; one who has made it still and steady — Says Nanak: the man who is of this kind, know him to be liberated. ॥2॥
685.2: Raag Dhanasari, by the Ninth Guru (Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji). Now what means shall I try, by which the mind's dread may end, (and) I may cross the terrifying world-ocean? Having gained (human) birth I have done no good; therefore I am greatly afraid. With mind, speech and deeds I have not sung the praises of the Lord: this worry I carry in my heart. Hearing the Guru's teaching, no wisdom at all has sprung up (in me); I fill my belly like a beast. Says Nanak: O God, (only if you) recognise (your own) birad (your age-old way of saving the fallen), can I, fallen as I am, cross over. ॥2॥
685.3: Raag Dhanasari, Ghar 2, Ashtapadis, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. The Guru is an ocean, brimful of jewels; the Sants peck the Amrit (from it), and do not stay far (from it). As it pleases God, they peck the feed of the Lord's essence; the swan (that stays) in the lake finds the Lord of its life. What does the poor crane gain by bathing in a puddle? It sinks into the mud, and its filth does not go. The thoughtful one sets down his feet with care upon care; leaving duality, (such ones) have become the Formless One's own. tasting the Lord's essence, (they have gained) the treasure of liberation; their comings and goings have ended: the Guru has kept them safe. The swan does not leave the lake and go; through loving devotion it merges in Sahaj. The swan is in the lake, and the ocean is in the swan; this is a story that cannot be told; through the Guru's words (it gains) honour. Some one yogi (rare, joined to God) sits in the realm of Sunn; (in that state) there is neither woman nor man: tell me, how could anyone describe (it)? he keeps his mind fixed on the Light that pervades the three worlds, the True One, in whose refuge are the gods, men and Naths (the masters of yoga). (He is) the source of bliss, the support of those who have none; through the Guru, by devotion (to him) and reflection, (one abides) in Sahaj. (He is) the lover of devotion, the dispeller of fears; killing Haumai and setting their feet (in the holy company), (the Gurmukhs) meet (him). Though many efforts are made, death torments (such a one); (such beings) have come into the world with death written (in their lot). (he) loses the treasure of (human) birth in duality; he does not know his own self, and wandering and wandering in doubt he weeps.
