(One who) speaks, reads and hears of the One alone (gains) patience and dharma, (and takes) the support of the Upholder of the earth; continence, truthful living and self-restraint come to dwell in (his) heart, if (his) mind is won over to the fourth state. To one made pure (by abiding) in the True One, no filth clings; through the Guru's Shabad, (his) doubt and fear run away. He whose form and being are from the beginning, beyond compare: Nanak begs for (him), the True One, whose form is eternal. ॥8॥
Ashtapadi (ashta, eight; pad, stanza): a hymn of about eight stanzas.

The lake and the swan: in Indian poetry the swan lives on the lake Mansarovar and feeds on pearls, and the crane, white outside but lying in wait for fish, is the image of the hypocrite; here the lake is the Guru and the swan the Guru's Sikh.
Sunn Mandal: the realm of Sunn, the stillness where no stirring of Maya arises. The Naths: the perfected masters of the yogis, such as Gorakhnath.
The fourth state (turiya): the spiritual state beyond Maya's three qualities.
686.1: Raag Dhanasari, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). One who meets (God) in Sahaj: his meeting is accepted; for him there is no dying, no coming and going. The servant is (merged) in the Master, and he (the Master) in the servant; wherever I look, there is no other. Through the Guru, by devotion, the home of Sahaj is found; without meeting the Guru, one dies (in spirit) and keeps coming and going. I take him alone as Guru who makes the True One firm (in the heart), (who) has (me) speak of the Indescribable One, (and) unites (me with him) through the Shabad. The Lord's people have no other task; the True Master, the True One, (alone) is dear (to them). The mind (stays) within the body, and within the mind is the True One; that (servant), made true, meeting the True One, is absorbed (in him). (That) servant falls at God's feet (whom) the perfect True Guru meets and unites (with God). (God) himself grants the sight (of himself), and he himself watches (over all); he is not won by stubborn force, nor by many garbs. He who fashioned the vessels (the bodies) and poured Amrit (into them): it is that God who has won (the mortal's) mind to loving devotion. Reading and reading, (people) go astray and suffer blows; through much cleverness they keep coming and going. One who repeats the Naam and eats the food of (God's) fear: (such) servants, through the Guru, stay merged (in God). Worshipping stones, (bathing at) places of pilgrimage, dwelling in the forests, wandering and wavering, (some) have become renunciants; (but) with the mind soiled, how can (one) be pure? one who merges in the True One: he alone receives honour. (Unite me with the Guru) in whose being are (true) conduct and reflection, whose mind, from the beginning and through the ages, is steady in Sahaj, who saves millions in the blink of an eye: in your grace, O Beloved, unite (me) with (that) Guru. Before whom, O God, should I praise you? Apart from you, (I see) no other. As it pleases you, so keep (me) in your will; so that Nanak may sing (your) praises in Sahaj, in love. ॥8॥
686.2: Raag Dhanasari, Ghar 6, an Ashtapadi, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. Whatever species (the soul) was born into, in that it was entangled; it has gained human birth by good fortune. O Saadh (the Guru), I have looked to your shelter: give (me) your hand and save (me); in your grace unite (me) with the Lord, the King. Wandering through countless births, I have found no resting place. O Guru, I serve (you) and fall at (your) feet: show (me), revered one, the path to Govind ji. I make countless efforts for Maya, I hold it close in my mind; (my life) ever passes in crying mine, mine. O brother, if only I might meet such a Sant, who would take away all my anxiety (and) attach my love to the Master. O brother, (I) have read all the Vedas, (yet) the mind's distance (from God) does not end; the five (senses) of my (body-) house are not at rest even for an instant. O brother, (if only I might meet) such a devotee, free of Maya, who would water my heart with the one Amrit Name. O brother, all the places of pilgrimage (one) bathed at only left the filth of the ego-bound intellect; the Master of the house (of the heart) is not pleased by them in the least. When shall I find the Saadh Sangat, (where) there is ever bliss in the Lord, Har Har, (and where) my mind may bathe in the collyrium of wisdom? All the ashrams (and their duties) have been kept, (yet) the mind is not satisfied; lacking discernment, (people only) wash the body. O brother, if only one might find such a being, the very form of the Creator, dyed in the love of the Supreme Lord, who would wash the filth of evil understanding from my mind. (One) caught up in the rituals of religion does not love (God) even for a moment; he falls into pride again and again, (and what he does) counts for nothing. One who meets the Guru, whose very form bears fruit, ever sings (God's) praise; by the Guru's grace some rare one sees (God) with his own eyes. What one works at by the mind's stubbornness is not counted in the least; like a crane he sits in meditation, but, O brother, he holds on to Maya. O brother, (if only I might meet) such a giver of peace, who would tell (me) the story of God: meeting him, our liberation would come. Gopal, the King, well pleased, cuts, O brother, the bonds of Maya; my mind is dyed in the Guru's Shabad. I have met fearless Gobind, and there is bliss for ever and ever; Nanak has fallen at the Lord's feet and found peace. Fruitful, fruitful, fruitful has (my life's) journey become; meeting the Saadh (the Guru), (my) comings and goings have ended. ॥1॥

The four ashrams: in Hindu custom the four stages of life, the student (brahmacharya), the householder (grihasth), the forest-dweller (vanaprasth) and the renunciant (sannyas), each with its own duties.
Rahao Dooja: the second Rahao (Pause) of this ashtapadi, which answers the prayer of the first.
687.1: Raag Dhanasari, Chhants, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. I go to bathe at a place of pilgrimage: (my) place of pilgrimage is the Naam. The place of pilgrimage is reflection on the Shabad, and the knowledge (of God) within. The Guru's wisdom is the true place of pilgrimage; it is (my) ten holy days, and ever (my) Dasahara. I ever beg for the Name of the Lord: give (it to me), O God, upholder of the earth. The world is sick, and the Naam is (its) remedy; without the True (Lord), filth clings (to the mind). The Guru's word is pure, a light that ever shines; it is the true place of pilgrimage and the daily bath. Joined to the True One, (the mind) gathers no filth; what filth is there to wash away? Having strung the garland of (the Lord's) virtues, before whom need one weep? One who, through reflection (on the Shabad), slays (his mind) crosses over and carries (others) across; he does not come back into the womb again. He himself becomes the paaras, one of the highest meditation; true, he pleases the True One. Bliss is his night and day, and true joy; he casts off pain and sins. He has found the True Name; the Guru has shown (him the Lord); no filth is on the mind set on the True One. Union with the Friend (the Lord) in the Sangat is the perfect bath. The singer who sings (the Lord's praise) is made beautiful through the Shabad. Praising the True One and trusting the True Guru, (one's) mind turns to good deeds, giving and compassion. Whoever, in the Husband's company, is pleasing (to him) and bathes in Sahaj, for him this is the confluence at Beni, purest of the pure. Worship the True Ekankar, the One Creator, who gives every day, and (whose gift) grows ever greater. In the company of the Friend, in the Sant Sangat, the highest state is reached; casting his glance of grace, (the Lord) has united (one) in his union. Everyone speaks of (him); how great can he be called? I am a fool, lowly and unknowing; by the teaching (of the Guru) I come to understand. True is the Guru's teaching, uttered as Amrit; in it my mind has come to trust. (People) depart and come (again), loaded with poison; through the True Shabad, my Guru (lifts that load). Telling (of him) never comes to an end, nor (does) devotion in (his) storehouses; he alone fills and pervades all. O Nanak, whoever utters the True One and offers prayer scours his mind, and (sees) that True One alone. ॥4॥
Chhant: a song of longer stanzas.

The ten parbs (das purab): by the Darpan, the ten holy days of the calendar, such as the new moon, the full moon, the first day of the month (sangrand) and the eclipses of sun and moon. Dasahara (das, ten; hara, taking away), the day held to take away ten sins, is the tenth of the bright half of Jeth, kept as the birthday of the Ganga.
Beni (Triveni): the meeting of the Ganga, the Jamuna and the Saraswati at Prayag, counted a great place of holy bathing.
688.1: Raag Dhanasari, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). I live by your Name; there is bliss in (my) mind. True, ever true, is (your) Name; Govind is the treasure of virtues. Through the Guru's wisdom (I know): the Creator is boundless; he who created (the world) is he who destroys (it). The summons (of death) has come, sent by (his) Hukam; no one can turn it back. He himself creates and watches over (all), writes (the writ) on every head, and himself gives understanding. Says Nanak: the Master is beyond reach and beyond the senses; I live by (his) true glory. There is none equal to you; whoever has come will go. By (your) Hukam the account (of birth and death) is settled; (the Guru) will remove the doubt. The Guru removes doubt and has (one) utter (the praise of) the Indescribable; (that one), true, merges in the True One. (God) himself creates and himself takes (all) back into himself; (that one) has recognised the Hukam of the Commander. True glory has been gained from the Guru; (O Lord,) you (dwell) in (that one's) mind, a companion at the end. O Nanak, there is no other Master besides (him); (O Lord,) glory lies in your Name. You are the true Creator, O unseen Maker. The Master is One; there are two paths, and strife grows. (He) has set both paths going; all are under (his) Hukam; the world is born and dies. Without the Naam there is no friend; (the world) has loaded itself with poison, a burden on its head. (One) has come by (his) Hukam, yet does not understand the Hukam; (the Lord) by (his) Hukam is the one who sets (him) right. O Nanak, through the Shabad the Master, the true Creator, is recognised. The devotees shine at (the Lord's) court, made beautiful by the Shabad. They speak the Bani of Amrit, their tongues steeped in (its) savour. Their tongues steeped (in it), they thirst for the Naam; through the Guru's Shabad they are sold (to the Lord). Touching the paaras, they become the paaras, when (O Lord) they are pleasing to your mind. They have reached the deathless state and lost (their) self; rare is one who reflects on (such) wisdom. O Nanak, the devotees shine at the door of the True One; they deal in the True (Name). Hungry and thirsty for wealth (Maya), how shall I go to (his) door? I go and ask the True Guru, and (by his counsel) I shall meditate on the Naam. I shall meditate on the True Name, speak of the True One, and through the Guru recognise the True One. Night and day I shall utter the Name of the Master of the lowly, the merciful, the stainless One. (The one for whom) the work worth doing is ordained from the source subdues the mind and himself dies (to self). O Nanak, the Naam is the highest and sweetest relish; by the Naam craving has been put away. ॥5॥
Many lines of these Chhants close with ਜੀਉ (jeeo), a word of loving address that rounds off the line; it adds nothing to the sense.
689.1: Raag Dhanasari, Chhants, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). The Husband is beside (you), O robbed bride, yet you have had no word of (him). On (your) forehead is written the writ (of what you) earned before. The writ earned before is not erased; what do I know of what is yet to be? (She who is) not virtuous, not of good conduct, not dyed in (his) love, will sit and weep again and again over (her) faults. Wealth and youth are the akk's (swallow-wort's) shade; old age comes, and the days run out. O Nanak, without the Name the wife her husband has forsaken is cast off; through falsehood she is parted (from him). O drowning one, you have laid waste (your) home; walk in the love of the Guru. Meditating on the True Name, you shall find (his) mansion and dwell there in peace. If she meditates on the Lord's Name, then she finds peace; in her parents' home (this world) are only four days. She goes and sits in her own home, finds the True One, and is with the Beloved night and day. Without devotion there is no dwelling in (that) home; listen, all you people! O Nanak, she, full of delight, finds the Husband then, (when she is) dyed in the True Name. When the Husband is dear to the bride, then the bride is dear to the Husband. Dyed in the love of the Beloved, she becomes thoughtful through the Guru's Shabad. Reflecting on the Guru's Shabad, dear to her Lord, she bows low again and again in devotion. The Beloved burns away (her) attachment to Maya, and in (his) sweetness she delights in (his) love. Dyed in the colour of love with the True Lord, she has subdued her mind and become lovely. O Nanak, the happy wife abides in the True One; in love with the Husband, she is dear (to him). The bride shines in the Husband's home if she pleases the Husband. (If) she speaks false words, (her speaking) is of no use. She speaks falsehood, which is of no use; she does not behold the Husband with her eyes. Full of faults, forgotten by the Husband, she is cast off; (her) night (of life passes) without her lord. She does not heed the Guru's Shabad; caught in the noose, that bride does not reach the mansion. O Nanak, (she who) recognises her own self merges, through the Guru, in Sahaj. Blessed is the happy wife who has come to know the Husband. Without the Name, the false one has earned only falsehood. Made beautiful by devotion to the Lord, she is dear to the True One; she is dyed in love and devotion for God. The Husband is the source of joy, ever young; dyed in (his) love, she enjoys (union with) him. Blossoming through the Guru's Shabad, she enjoys her Lord; she has obtained the fruit that brings virtues. O Nanak, she meets the True One and gains glory; the bride shines in the Husband's home. ॥5॥
The akk (swallow-wort) is a low wild shrub; its shade is scant and soon gone.
Pir dhan bhavai ta pir bhavai nari: pir with aunkar (ਪਿਰੁ) is the subject, the Husband who is dear to the bride; pir without it (ਪਿਰ) means to the Husband.
690.1: Raag Dhanasari, Ghar 1, Chhants, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. If the dear Lord shows his grace, then one can meditate on the Naam. (If) the True Guru is met, then in love and in Sahaj one can sing (his) praises. Singing (his) praises, one blossoms ever, night and day, when it pleases the True One himself. He gives up pride, Haumai and Maya, and in Sahaj merges in the Naam. The Creator himself does (this); when he himself gives, then (the gift) is received. If the dear Lord shows his grace, then one can meditate on the Naam. True love for the Perfect True Guru dwells within (me). Day and night I serve him; he never slips from my mind. I never forget (him), and keep (him) close night and day; whenever I take the Name, I live. When I hear (it) with my ears, this mind is satisfied; through the Guru I drink the Amrit. When (the Lord) casts his glance of grace, then he unites (one) with the True Guru; night and day the discerning intellect is at work. True love for the Perfect True Guru dwells within (me). When the Sat Sangat is found by great good fortune, then the savour of the Lord comes. (One) stays attuned night and day, and so merges in Sahaj. When he merges in Sahaj, he pleases the Lord's mind; he is ever beyond (Maya), detached. In this world and the next, throughout the world, (he has) honour; his mind is attuned to the Name of Ram. He is free of both joy and sorrow; whatever God does pleases him. When the Sat Sangat is found by great good fortune, then the savour of the Lord comes. In the love of another there is suffering; Jam has the manmukh in his sight. He cries alas, alas, day and night, ensnared in the pain of Maya. Ensnared in the pain of Maya, enraged through Haumai, he passes (his life) crying mine, mine. The God who gives (all), him he does not remember; at the end he departs in regret. Without the Name no one goes along; he is deceived by sons, wife and Maya. In the love of another there is suffering; Jam has the manmukh in his sight. The one whom you, in your grace, unite (with yourself) has found the mansion of the Lord. He stays ever with palms joined; God has become dear to his mind. When God is dear to the mind, then one merges in (his) Hukam; obeying the Hukam, he has found peace. Every day, day and night, he keeps repeating (the Name); in Sahaj he has meditated on the Naam. The Name, the Name alone, is the glory he has received; O Nanak, the Name is dear to (his) mind. The one whom you, in your grace, unite (with yourself) finds the mansion of the Lord. ॥5॥
691.1: Raag Dhanasari, Chhants, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. Merciful to the lowly is the True Guru, in whose company the Lord is sung. The Lord's Name is Amrit; in the Saadh Sangat it is savoured. Go to the company of the Saadh and dwell on the One; the pain of birth and death is destroyed. (One for whom) grace was written from the first has learned the True (Name); the noose of Jam is cut. Fears and doubts have fled, the knot is untied; one never comes upon the path of Jam. Nanak prays: show mercy, that we may ever sing the praises of the Lord. The one support of the supportless is the Name of the Stainless (Lord). You are the Giver, the Bountiful One, destroyer of every pain. O remover of pain, Creator, Master of peace: whoever has come to the refuge of the Saadh, him you have carried across the dreadful world-ocean in a single moment. You fill every place, (seen by one who has) the Guru's wisdom as salve in the eyes. Nanak prays: may I ever remember (you), the destroyer of all pain and fear. Showing mercy, you yourself have attached (your own) to your hem. I am without virtue, lowly and without a master, O God, unfathomable and boundless. O merciful Master, ever kind, who raises up the lowly, all beings and creatures are in your power; all are in your care. You yourself are the Creator, you yourself the enjoyer, you yourself consider all. Nanak prays: singing (your) praises, may I live; may I repeat the chant of the Lord, O Banwari. The sight of you is boundless, (your) Name priceless. Your servants repeat (it) ever, O immeasurable Purakh. You have come to dwell on the tongues of the Sants, pleased of yourself; they alone are intoxicated with the Lord's savour. Those of great fortune who cling to the Guru's feet stay awake always, night and day. Ever and ever (the Saadh) utters, with every breath, the praises of the Master who is to be remembered: Nanak prays: (give me) the dust of (such a) Saadh, O God; (your) Name is priceless. ॥4॥
691.2: Raag Dhanasari, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji. Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. Those like Sanak, Sanand and Mahesh (Shiv), and Shesh Nag have not known your secret. In the company of the Sants, I enshrine Ram in (my) heart. Those like Hanuman, those like Garur, the lord of the gods (Indra) and the kings of men have not known (your) virtues. The four Vedas, the Simritis and the Puranas, Kamlapati (Vishnu) and Kavla (Lakshmi) have not known (you). Says Kabir: that one does not wander in doubt who, clinging to the feet (of the Sants), stays in the refuge of Ram. ॥4॥

Sanak and Sanand (Sanandan): two of the four sons of Brahma in the Puranas (Sanak, Sanandan, Sanatan and Sanat Kumar), sages held to remain children for ever. Shesh Nag: the thousand-headed serpent of the Puranas, held to utter a new Name of God with every tongue.
Hanuman is the servant of Ram; Garur (Garuda), the king of birds, is the mount of Vishnu.
692.1: From days into watches, from watches into moments, life runs down and the body wastes away; death, the hunter, prowls like a slayer of game; tell me, what way is there (to escape)? That day has begun to draw near; mother, father, brother, son and wife: tell me, is anyone anyone's own? As long as the light (of life) abides in the body, the beast (that man is) does not know himself; he greedily craves the state of living on, and his eyes see nothing. Says Kabir: listen, O mortal, give up the delusions of the mind; repeat the Naam alone, O mortal, and fall into the refuge of the One. ॥3॥
692.2: For one who knows anything of loving devotion, what is there (in this) to wonder at? As water that enters water does not come out again, so the weaver, his self melted away, has merged (in the Lord). O people of the Lord, I am simple in understanding. If you, Kabir, give up your body in Kashi, what favour would the all-pervading Lord have done (in your release)? Says Kabir: listen, O people: let none of you go astray in delusion; what is Kashi, and what the barren Magahar, if Ram is in the heart? ॥2॥

Kashi (Banaras), Shiva's city, was believed to free whoever died there, and Magahar to send whoever died there into birth as a donkey; to break this belief, Kabir left Kashi in old age to live and die at Magahar.
692.3: (Though one) should reach the realm of Indra or the realm of Shiva, (having got there) by petty austerities, one will come back again. What shall I ask for? Nothing is lasting. Keep the Name of Ram within your mind. Renown, kingship, splendour and greatness: at the end, none of these goes with anyone as a helper. Sons, wife, riches and Maya: tell me, who has found peace in these? Says Kabir: all else is of no use; for my mind, the (true) wealth is the Name of Ram. ॥4॥
692.4: Remember Ram, remember Ram, remember Ram, O brother. Without remembrance of the Name of Ram, a great many are drowning. Wife, sons, body, house and wealth, (which seem) to give comfort: none of these is yours when the appointed hour of death has come. Ajamal, Gaj the elephant and Ganika did sinful deeds, (yet) they too crossed over to the far shore by taking the Name of Ram. You have wandered through births as swine and dog, and still you felt no shame; why do you leave the Amrit of Ram's Name and eat poison? Give up the delusion of rites enjoined and forbidden (by the scriptures), and take the Name of Ram. By the Guru's grace, O servant Kabir, make Ram your loving friend. ॥4॥

Ajamal: a fallen Brahmin, saved when at death he called on his son Narayan. Gaj: in the Bhagavat Purana, an elephant seized in the water by a crocodile; when his strength failed he called on the Lord and was set free. Ganika: a courtesan, saved by teaching a parrot to say Ram.
692.5: Raag Dhanasari, the hymn of Bhagat Namdev Ji. Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. (People) had deep foundations dug and raised mansions upon them; (yet) who was greater in years than Markandeya, who passed his days with only straw above his head? The Creator, Ram, is our loving friend. O men, why do you take pride? This false body will perish. The Kaurav brothers, such as Duryodhan, kept saying mine, mine; their royal canopy reached over twelve jojans, yet vultures ate their bodies. All Lanka was of gold, (its lord) one as mighty as Ravan; what came of the elephants tethered at his door? In a moment (Lanka) passed to another. The Yadavs played a trick on Durbasa and reaped this fruit. (The Lord) has shown grace to his own servant, and Namdev sings the Lord's praises. ॥4॥
Markandeya: a sage of the Puranas, held to have lived an exceedingly long life, who yet spent it all in a hut of straw.

The Kauravs: in the Mahabharata, the sons of King Dhritarashtra, Duryodhan the eldest, slain by the Pandavas in the war at Kurukshetra. A jojan (yojana) is about four kos; the royal canopy (chhatar) is the sign of sovereignty.

Durbasa: a sage quick to anger and to curse. Youths of the Yadavs (Krishna's clan) dressed a boy as a pregnant woman and asked him in mockery what she would bear; by his curse the whole Yadav clan fell to fighting among themselves and perished.
693.1: I have brought the ten (senses) under my control, made free of desire; the very name of the five (passions) is wiped out. The seventy-two (thousand channels of the body) I have filled from the pool of Amrit, and the poison I kill and drive out. I shall not come back (into birth) again, (for) from my heart I utter the Amrit Bani and instruct my own self. Making entreaty and falling at (the Guru's) feet, I have wrested away the hard axe (of death); turned around, I am now the servant of the Sants, and I stand in awe of the devotees. I am free of this world only when I do not cling to Maya; Maya is but another name for birth in the womb; giving it up, I gain the sight (of the Lord). Those who worship in this way are rid of all fear. Says Namdev: why do you wander outside? By these disciplines the Lord is found. ॥4॥

The ten: the ten senses, of perception and of action; the five: lust, anger, greed, attachment and pride. Satar doi (seventy and two): by yogic lore, the seventy-two thousand channels (nadis) of the body.
693.2: As water is dear in Marwar (the land of sand), as the creeper is dear to the camel, as the sound (of the hunter's bell) at night is dear to the deer, so dear to my mind is the beautiful Ram. Beautiful is your Name, beautiful your form, and beautiful beyond measure your colour, O my beautiful Ram. As Indra (the rain) is dear to the earth, as the fragrance of the flower to the bumblebee, as the mango is dear to the koel, so dear to my mind is the beautiful Ram. As the sun is dear to the chakvi, (as) Mansarovar to the swan, as her husband is dear to a young woman, so dear to my mind is the beautiful Ram. As milk is dear to a child, as the cloud to the mouth of the chatrik, as water is dear to the fish, so dear to my mind is the beautiful Ram. Seekers, Siddhas and all the sages long (for him), but rare is the one who has seen (him). As your Name is dear to all the worlds, so is Bithal dear to Nama's mind. ॥5॥
The chakvi (ruddy shelduck), parted from her mate at night, waits all night for the sunrise.
693.3: In the very beginning (the world arose like) a forest of white lotuses; all beings are its swans. Know that it is from Krishna (the Lord who draws all) that the Lord's dancing creation dances. First of all, the Purakh (the Primal Being) himself became manifest, then from the Purakh came Maya; (all this is the union) of this one (Maya) and of that one (the Purakh): the Lord's fair garden dances like the water in the pots (of a Persian wheel). Women and men are dancing, (but) none is apart from the Master. Have no doubt (of this), (and cast off) delusion: in every woman and man it is the word of Keshav (the Lord) alone that runs, one and the same. Like the pots (of a Persian wheel), beings rise and sink in the world; after long wandering I have come to your door. (You ask:) Who are you? I, O Lord, am Nama. O Lord, save me from the snare of the house (of the world), the root of (the fear of) Jam. ॥3॥

In this shabad Namdev uses Marathi and Sanskrit words: che (of), pundarak (the white lotus), krisna (the Lord who draws all), pursabira (the Purakh became manifest), pursadamra (from the Purakh, Maya), pindhi (the pots of a Persian wheel), naiya (the leader, the Lord), ala (the house, the world's snare).
694.1: O Madho, to make the fallen pure is your age-old way. Blessed are those sages who have meditated on my Lord God. The dust of Gobind's feet has touched my forehead, (dust that is) far even from gods, men and sages. O Madho, merciful to the lowly, destroyer of pride, Nama has taken the refuge of your feet and is a sacrifice to you. ॥2॥
694.2: Raag Dhanasari, the hymn of Bhagat Ravidas Ji. Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. There is none as lowly as I, and none as merciful as you; what more testing (of this) is needed now? That my mind may be won by your words, grant your servant this (faith) in full. O dear Ram, I am a sacrifice, ever a sacrifice, to you; for what reason do you not speak (to me)? For many births I was parted (from you), O Madho; this birth is given over to you. Says Ravidas: I live on hope alone; it is long since I saw you. ॥2॥
694.3: In my mind I remember (you), with my eyes I behold (you), and I keep my ears filled with (your) Bani and your fair praise; my mind I make the bumblebee, (your) feet I hold in my heart, and with my tongue I utter the Amrit Name of Ram. May my love for Gobind never grow less; I have bought it at a heavy price, in exchange for my life. Without the Saadh Sangat, love does not arise, and without love your devotion cannot be. Ravidas makes one prayer to the Lord: keep my honour, O Ram, Sovereign Lord. ॥2॥
694.4: Your Name, O Murari, is (my) aarti and (my) bath of pilgrimage. Without the Lord's Name, all display is false. Your Name is (my) seat, your Name the stone for grinding (sandal), your Name the saffron I take and sprinkle (upon you); your Name is the water, your Name the sandalwood; to repeat the Name is to grind it, and this Name I take and offer to you. Your Name is the lamp, your Name the wick, your Name the oil that I take and pour into it; I have lit the flame of your Name, and all the worlds are filled with light. Your Name is the thread, the Name the flowers and the garland; the eighteen loads of plant life are all defiled. What can I offer you of what you yourself have made? Your Name is the fly-whisk that I wave over you. The eighteen (Puranas), the sixty-eight (places of pilgrimage) and the four sources of life: in these the whole world is occupied. Says Ravidas: your Name is (my) aarti; the True Name, O Lord, is the food offered to you (bhog). ॥4॥
The eighteen loads: all plant life; an old belief holds that one leaf of every kind of tree and plant, weighed together, comes to eighteen bhaar (an old measure of weight).

Das atha (ten and eight): the eighteen Puranas; athsathe: the sixty-eight places of pilgrimage, the tiraths held most holy in India; the four sources of life (khaani): birth from the egg, from the womb, from sweat and from the earth. Bhog: the food set before the deity in worship.
695.1: Raag Dhanasari, the hymns of the Bhagats: the hymn of Bhagat Trilochan Ji. Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. Why do you find fault with Narayan, O foolish one gone astray? Evil deeds and good deeds are your own doing, O dear one. (The moon) dwells on the brow of Shankar (Shiva) and bathes in the Ganga, O brother; in the people of its line the bearer of the bow (Vishnu) was born, O brother; (yet) because of its own deeds the stain did not leave it, O dear one. The lamp of the world (the sun) is his master, O brother, (he is its) charioteer, and Garur, king of birds, is his kinsman; (yet) because of his deeds Arun is lame, O dear one. The remover of countless sins, lord of the three worlds (Shiva), wandered from tirath to tirath and found no release, O dear one; because of his deeds the skull did not leave (his hand), O dear one. Amrit, the moon, the cow of plenty, Lakshmi, the wish-granting tree, the long-eared horse and the skilled (physician Dhanvantar came from) the lord of rivers (the ocean); (yet) because of its deeds its saltiness did not leave it, O dear one. (Hanuman) burned the fort of Lanka, uprooted Ravan's garden, and brought the herb that heals wounds to please Hari (Ram Chandar); (yet) because of his deeds his loincloth did not leave him, O dear one. Deeds done before are not erased (by such means), O mistress of the house; that is why I repeat the Name of Ram. Says Trilochan: (I repeat) Ram Ji (alone). ॥6॥

The Puranic stories: the moon bears a stain for its misdeed, by the curse of the sage Gautam; it sits on Shiva's brow, and Krishna, Vishnu's incarnation, was born in the lunar line. Arun, the dawn, Garur's elder brother and the sun's charioteer, was born lame. Shiva cut off one of Brahma's heads, and the skull clung to his hand until it fell away at the tirath of Kapal-mochan. The ocean yielded fourteen jewels when it was churned, and is salt still. Hanuman, for all his service to Ram, had only a loincloth.
Re (masculine) and ri (feminine) are words of address.
695.2: Raag Dhanasari, the hymn of Sri Sain Ji. (My) aarti, made ready with incense, lamps and ghee, (is this): I am a sacrifice to you, O Lord of Kamla. Bliss, O Lord, bliss: the bliss of Ram, the Sovereign King, is (within me) always. The finest lamp and the purest wick are you alone, the stainless one, O Lord of Kamla. Through devotion to Ram, one comes to know the bliss of Ram, (one who) speaks the praise of the all-pervading Lord, the supreme bliss. The Lord of enchanting form, who carries (us) across all fears, Gobind: says Sain, worship (him), the Lord of supreme bliss. ॥4॥
Kamla pati (Lakshmi's husband): a name of Vishnu; here the one Lord.
695.3: Raag Dhanasari, the hymn of Bhagat Pipa Ji. The body itself is the deity, the body itself the temple, the body itself the wandering Jangam and the pilgrim; the body itself is the incense, the lamp and the food offered; in the body itself I worship, with my offering of leaves. After searching many lands, I have found the nine treasures within the body. Now nothing will come and nothing will go; it is Ram's glory that reigns. He who is in the universe is the same in the body; whoever searches finds (him). Pipa humbly prays: (the Lord) is the supreme essence; when the True Guru is found, he makes (him) seen. ॥2॥
Jangams are Shaiva mendicants who go about ringing bells.
695.4: Raag Dhanasari, the hymn of Bhagat Dhanna Ji. O Gopal, I am a needy one at your door; those who worship you, you set right their affairs. I ask for lentils, flour and ghee, that my heart may be glad each day; shoes and fine clothing, and I ask for grain from a field ploughed seven times. I ask for a cow and a buffalo in milk, a fine Arab mare, and a good wife for the home: these servant Dhanna asks of you and receives. ॥2॥
Aarta (Sanskrit arta): afflicted, in need; it is not aarti. Sat si: (a field) ploughed seven times.

660.1: Raag Dhanasari, Ghar 1, Chaupade, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).

There is one God, Ik Oankar, the One who pervades all and is ever the same; his Name is Sat (the One who truly is); he is the Creator, the Being who dwells in all, without fear, without enmity, his form beyond time, unborn, self-existent, realised by the Guru's grace.
My own soul is afraid; to whom shall I cry out?
I have served the one who makes sorrow forgotten, the Giver for ever and ever.
My Master is ever new; he is the Giver for ever and ever.
Night and day let us serve the Master; in the end it is he who sets us free.
Hearing (his Name) again and again, O my soul-bride, one is carried across.
O Merciful One, may I cross over through your Name;
I am for ever a sacrifice (to you).
The One True Lord is in every place; there is none besides him.
Only the one on whom he casts his glance of grace serves him.
Without you, O Beloved, how can I live?
Grant me that greatness by which I may stay attached to your Name.
O Beloved, there is no one else before whom I could go and say it.
I serve my own Master; I beg of no one else.
Nanak is his servant, and moment by moment he is offered up to him, piece by piece.
O Master, moment by moment (Nanak) is offered up to your Name, piece by piece. ॥4॥
660.2: Raag Dhanasari, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
We humans are of a single breath; we know neither the term (of our life) nor the moment (of death).
Nanak prays: serve him alone to whom the soul and the breath of life belong.
O blind one, consider and see: how many days does (this) life last?
(O Lord,) breath, flesh, soul, all are yours; you are deeply dear to me.
Thus says Nanak, the poet, O True Sustainer.
If you give nothing to someone, O my Master, what can he bring out to offer as a pledge?
Nanak prays: one receives just that which is due by what was written before.
The deceitful one did not keep the Master's Name in his mind; he practised deceit.
When he was seized and driven to the door of Jam (the messenger of Death), then he went, repenting.
As long as we remain in the world, O Nanak, let us hear something (of the Lord) and say something.
We have searched to weariness and found no lasting stay (here); let us live as those who have died while yet alive. ॥5॥
661.1: Raag Dhanasari, Ghar 2, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
How shall I remember him? (By my own effort) he cannot be remembered.
(Without him) my heart burns, and my soul cries out in pain.
That True One himself creates and adorns;
if he is forgotten, how can any good come?
He is not found by cleverness or by giving orders;
how, then, may I meet the True One, O my mother?
Only a rare one goes to look at the merchandise of the Naam (the Name, God's presence remembered);
none tastes it, none eats it.
Winning people over brings no honour;
honour stays only when he himself preserves it.
Wherever I look, there he is, pervading.
(O Lord,) apart from you there is no other place.
If anyone tries (by his own effort), what comes of his doing?
(it comes to) the one on whom that True One bestows it.
Soon (I) must rise and depart, in a moment or in a single beat of time;
what face shall I show? I have no virtues with me.
As is the glance he casts, so does one become;
without the glance of his grace, O Nanak, none is anything. ॥4॥
661.2: Raag Dhanasari, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
When (God) casts his glance of grace, then he can be remembered;
(then) the soul melts and (one) stays attuned (to him) in loving attention.
One makes the soul and the Supreme Soul one,
and the duality within dies within.
By the Guru's grace (God) is found;
when the mind is attached to the Lord, death devours (one) no more.
When the True One is remembered, light dawns (within),
and by it one remains detached even in the midst of the poison (of Maya).
Such is the greatness of the True Guru
that among sons and wife one attains the highest state.
The servant does such service
that he lays his soul before him whose it is.
He who pleases the Master is accepted;
that servant receives honour in the Lord's court.
The servant who enshrines the True Guru's form in his heart
obtains whatever fruit he desires.
The True Master shows him mercy;
why should such a servant fear Jam?
Says Nanak, when one reflects (on the Word)
and enshrines love for the true Bani,
only then does one find the door of liberation.
This Shabad is all chanting and austerity; it is the most excellent. ॥5॥
661.3: Raag Dhanasari, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
The soul burns again and again;
burning and burning, it wears itself away in so many vices.
The body in which the (Lord's) Bani is forgotten
wails like one sick with a chronic disease.
Much speaking is mere babbling;
without our speaking, he knows everything.
He who made the ears, the eyes and the nose,
who gave the tongue that speaks so swiftly,
who placed the mind in the fire (of the womb) and kept it safe,
(by whose power) the breath moves and one speaks in every place: (he is the one to remember).
All the attachment, the loves and the relishes (of the world)
are blackness, all of them, stain upon stain.
With the stains of faults on his face one departs,
and in the Lord's court there is no place for him to sit.
(O Lord,) only by (your) grace is the uttering of your Name received;
holding to it one crosses over; there is no other place.
Even if one is drowning, care is still taken of him (through the Name).
O Nanak, the True One gives to all. ॥4॥
662.1: Raag Dhanasari, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
If a thief offers praise, the heart is not moved;
if he speaks ill, (one) is not diminished by a hair.
No one stands surety for a thief.
How can one who is marked a thief be (taken for) good?
Listen, O blind mind, greedy as a dog, O false one:
without a word spoken, the true are recognised.
A thief may be handsome, a thief may be clever,
yet the counterfeit is worth no more than a dugana (a trifling coin).
If it is kept alongside (the genuine) and mixed in with them,
when it is tested, it proves false.
As one does, so one receives;
one sows and oneself eats (the harvest).
If one keeps singing one's own praises, (one does not become great by it);
as is one's inclination, so is the road one takes.
Though one may tell a hundred lies, falsehood and rubbish,
and though the whole world may call him (good),
(O Lord,) if it pleases you, the simple one is accepted.
O Nanak, the Knower, the all-wise, knows (all). ॥4॥
662.2: Raag Dhanasari, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
The body is the paper, and the mind the decree (written on it);
the ignorant one does not read the writ upon his head.
In the Lord's court three (kinds of) writ are engraved;
see, the false one is of no use.
O Nanak, if there is silver in (the coin),
everyone calls it genuine, genuine.
The qazi speaks falsehood and eats filth (ill-gotten gain);
the Brahmin takes his holy bath after slaying living beings;
the yogi, blind, does not know the way:
all three lay the groundwork of ruin.
He alone is a yogi who recognises the way
and, by the Guru's grace, knows the One.
He is a qazi who turns (his mind) back (from the world)
and, by the Guru's grace, dies while living.
He is a Brahmin who reflects on Brahm (God);
he himself swims across and carries all his families across.
He alone is wise who washes his heart clean;
he alone is a Muslim who rids himself of filth.
The learned one who understands is accepted,
he upon whose head is the mark of the Lord's court. ॥4॥
662.3: Raag Dhanasari, Ghar 3, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
It is not that age now; there is no yoga, nor any way of truth;
the world's places of worship have been defiled; in this way the world is drowning.
In Kalyug the Name of Ram is the most excellent of all.
They shut their eyes and hold their noses, (but all) to cheat the world.
They pinch their noses with thumb and fingers (and claim) they see the three worlds;
yet they see nothing of what lies behind their backs: this is a strange lotus posture.
The Kshatriyas have abandoned their dharma and taken up the language of the mlechhas;
the whole world has become of one varna, and the order of dharma has come to an end.
(The pandits) compose the eight (works of grammar), study the Puranas and practise the Vedas;
(but) says servant Nanak: without the Lord's Name there is no liberation. ॥4॥
663.1: Raag Dhanasari, Aarti, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
The sky is the platter; the sun and the moon are its lamps, and the clusters of stars are like pearls;
the sandal-scented breeze from the Malaya hills is the incense, the wind waves the fly-whisk, and all the plant life blossoms for the Light (that is God).
What a wondrous aarti this is! O Destroyer of the round of births, this is your aarti:
the unstruck sound resounds as its drums.
Thousands are your eyes, yet you have no eye; thousands are your forms, yet not one form is yours;
thousands are your spotless feet, yet you have not one foot; you are without a nose, yet thousands are your noses: these wonders of yours have enchanted me.
Within all is the light, and that light is he.
By his radiance there is light within all.
Through the Guru's teaching this light becomes manifest.
Whatever pleases him, that becomes the aarti.
My mind is lured by the nectar of the Lord's lotus feet; night and day I thirst for it.
Give Nanak, the rain-bird, the water of your grace, by which he may abide in your Name. ॥4॥
663.2: Raag Dhanasari, Ghar 2, Chaupade, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
This wealth (of the Name) is inexhaustible; it neither runs out nor is lost.
The perfect True Guru has shown it (to me).
To my own True Guru I am ever a sacrifice;
by the Guru's grace I enshrine the Lord in my mind.
They alone are rich who attune their love to the Name of the Lord;
the Perfect Guru has revealed the Lord's wealth (within them); by the Lord's grace it comes to dwell in the mind.
Failings are cut away and virtues settle in the heart
through the Perfect Guru, in Sahaj and in love.
The true Bani of the Perfect Guru
brings peace within the mind, and settles (there) in Sahaj.
Behold one wonder, O people, O brothers:
slaying duality, (the Guru) enshrines the Lord in the mind.
The Naam is priceless; it cannot be obtained (at any price);
by the Guru's grace it comes to dwell in the mind.
The One God dwells in all;
through the Guru's teaching he becomes manifest in the heart.
One who, in Sahaj, has known God and recognised him,
O Nanak, receives the Naam, and (his) mind is content. ॥4॥
664.1: Raag Dhanasari, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
The wealth of the Lord's Name is pure and utterly boundless;
through the Guru's Shabad its storehouses are filled.
Know that all else but the wealth of the Naam is poison;
in attachment to Maya the proud one burns.
Some rare one, through the Guru, tastes the Lord's sweet essence;
he is in bliss always, day and night; (this essence) is attained by perfect fortune.
The Shabad is a lamp, shining in the three worlds;
whoever tastes it becomes pure.
With the pure Naam he washes off the filth of Haumai,
and through true devotion there is peace for ever.
One who has tasted the Lord's sweet essence is the Lord's servant;
he has joy always, and never sorrow.
He himself is liberated, and he has others liberated too;
he repeats the Lord's Name, and from the Lord he receives peace.
Without the True Guru the whole (world) has died wailing;
night and day they burn, and (none) finds calm.
When the True Guru is met, he quenches all craving;
O Nanak, through the Naam one finds calm and peace. ॥4॥
664.2: Raag Dhanasari, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
The Naam is wealth for ever: cherish it within you,
(the Name of the One) who alone sustains all beings and creatures.
The treasure of liberation comes to those
who, attuning their love, stay dyed in the Lord's Name.
By serving the Guru one gains the wealth that is the Lord's Name;
there is light within (him), and he meditates on the Lord's Name.
This deep dye of the Lord, the Husband, comes upon the soul-bride
who has made peace her adornment; she enjoys that God.
In Haumai no one finds God;
strayed from the Root, one wastes one's life.
From the Guru, through the Bani, come calm and the peace of Sahaj;
true is (the Guru's) service, and through it one merges in the Naam.
Through the Shabad the Beloved is met, (and one) meditates on him ever;
through the True Name (one) receives glory.
The Creator himself is present, age after age;
when he casts his glance of grace, union (with him) comes about.
Through Gurbani one enshrines the Lord in the mind;
O Nanak, those dyed in the True One, God himself has united (with himself). ॥4॥
664.3: Raag Dhanasari, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
The world is soiled, and grows ever more soiled;
lured by another (than God), it comes and goes.
In the love of another all people are being ruined;
the manmukh suffers blows, and has lost his honour.
Through serving the Guru one becomes pure;
the Naam dwells within, and (one's) honour is exalted.
The Gurmukhs are saved in the Lord's refuge;
dyed in the Lord's Name, they have made devotion firm (in their hearts).
One who performs devotion receives glory;
dyed in the True One, they stay merged in peace and Sahaj.
Know that a buyer of the True One is rare;
(such a one) recognises his own self through the Guru's Shabad.
True is (his) capital, true (his) trade;
blessed is the person who has love for the Naam.
That True God has attached some to the Truth;
(to them) he makes the sublime Bani, the Shabad, heard.
True is the service of the True God;
O Nanak, through the Name he is the one who adorns (all). ॥4॥
665.1: Raag Dhanasari, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
To those who serve the Lord I am a sacrifice;
in their hearts is the Truth, and on their lips the True Name.
Cherish the True One, the True One alone, and sorrow departs;
through the true Shabad he comes to dwell in the mind.
Hearing Gurbani, one washes away (one's) filth,
and in Sahaj enshrines the Lord's Name in the mind.
He quenches falsehood, deceit and the fire of craving,
and finds calm within, and peace in Sahaj.
If one walks in the Guru's will, then self-conceit departs;
singing the Lord's praises, one finds the true mansion (of his presence).
One who neither understands the Shabad nor knows the Bani:
that blind manmukh's (life) passes in pain.
If one meets the True Guru, then one finds peace,
and holds Haumai in check within.
To whom else should one speak? That One alone is the Giver;
when he shows grace, union comes about through the Shabad.
Having met the Beloved (Guru), may I sing the True One's praises;
may Nanak, becoming true, be pleasing to the True One. ॥4॥
665.2: Raag Dhanasari, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
When the mind dies (to self), its wandering dies away;
without the mind dying, how can one find the Lord?
Rare is the one who knows the medicine by which this mind dies;
the mind dies through the Shabad: that one alone understands this.
The one whom the Lord forgives, he grants the glory
that, by the Guru's grace, he comes to dwell in the mind.
When, through the Guru, one practises the conduct worth practising,
then one comes to understand this mind.
The mind is drunk, like an elephant maddened by wine;
the Guru, striking it with the goad, brings it to life.
The mind is hard to tame; some rare one tames it.
When one consumes what will not yield (the mind's stubbornness), then (the mind) becomes pure.
Through the Guru, one has set this mind in order,
and casts Haumai and the vices out from within.
Those whom he has, from the very beginning, kept joined in his union
are never parted (from him); they stay merged in the Shabad.
God himself knows his own power;
O Nanak, through the Guru one recognises the Naam. ॥4॥
665.3: Raag Dhanasari, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Fools and the ignorant amass flimsy (perishable) wealth;
the manmukhs, blind and ignorant, have gone astray.
From the wealth of poisonous Maya there is ever pain;
it does not go along (at the end), nor is anything gained (by it).
One obtains the true wealth through the Guru's teaching;
flimsy wealth comes and goes again and again.
Astray, the ignorant manmukhs all die;
they drown in the world-ocean, (reaching) neither this shore nor the far shore.
(Those whom) the True Guru meets, by perfect fortune,
stay dyed in the True One, day and night, in bairag.
In all four ages the true Bani is Amrit;
by perfect fortune (through it one) merges in the Lord's Name.
The Siddhas and seekers, all in the world, long (for it);
(but) it is attained by perfect fortune alone.
Everything is the True One; he himself is true;
rare is the one who recognises that sublime Brahm (the Supreme Lord).
The True One, ever true, himself makes the Truth firm (in the heart);
O Nanak, (God) himself watches over (all), and himself attaches (them) to the Truth. ॥4॥
666.1: Raag Dhanasari, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
The worth and measure of the Name cannot be told;
blessed are those people who attune their love to the Name of the One.
True is the Guru's teaching, (and through it comes) reflection on the True One;
(God) himself forgives, and grants (this) reflection.
Wondrous is the Lord's Name; God himself makes it heard;
in this age of Kalyug, one obtains it through the Guru.
We are fools, utter fools in our minds;
(we) do all our deeds in Haumai.
By the Guru's grace Haumai departs;
(God) himself forgives and unites (one with himself).
The wealth of poisonous Maya (breeds) great pride;
in pride one drowns, and receives no honour.
When self-conceit is given up, there is peace for ever;
through the Guru's teaching I praise that True One.
That Creator himself fashions (the creation);
apart from him there is no other at all.
Only the one whom he attaches to the Truth is attached to it;
O Nanak, through the Naam there is peace for ever, hereafter (too). ॥4॥
666.2: Raag Dhanasari, Ghar 4, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
We are beggars, mendicants (at your door); you are your own Master, the Giver.
Be merciful and grant the Name to (me,) your begging servant, that I may stay ever dyed in (your) love.
I am a sacrifice to your True Name.
You alone are the root of creation, (the Maker) of all; there is no other, no second.
Many rounds (of birth) have fallen to (me,) the miser; now show (me) some mercy.
Be merciful and grant (me) the sight of yourself; bestow such a gift.
Says Nanak: the curtains of doubt have opened, and by the Guru's grace (God) is known;
a true love has taken hold within, and the mind has come to trust the True Guru. ॥3॥
666.3: Raag Dhanasari, Ghar 1, Chaupade, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
The Sants and devotees who serve the Lord: (the Lord) takes away all their sins.
Show mercy to us (too), O Master; keep (us) in the Sangat that is dear to you.
I cannot tell the Lord's virtues, O Banwari.
We sinners are stones sinking in water; in your mercy carry us stones across.
The poisonous rust that has clung through birth after birth is scoured away by clinging to the Saadh Sangat (the company of the holy),
as gold heated in the fire has its dross cut away and removed.
Day and night I repeat the Lord, Har Har; repeating (him), I keep the Lord, Har Har Har, in my heart.
The Lord, Har Har Har, is the perfect medicine in the world; repeating the Lord, Har Har, Haumai is slain.
O Lord, Har Har, inaccessible, unfathomable to understanding, beyond the farthest, O infinite Being,
show mercy to your servant, O Life of the world, and uphold the honour of servant Nanak. ॥4॥
667.1: Raag Dhanasari, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
The Lord's Sants who have repeated (the Name of) the Lord: their pain, doubt and fear have fled.
(God) himself has had them do his service, and the Guru's teaching has awakened within them.
One imbued with the Lord's Name is a bairagi, detached (from Maya).
He has heard the telling of the Lord, Har Har, and it pleases his mind; through the Guru's teaching his love is fixed on the Lord.
O Lord and Master, (you are) the caste of your Sants; you are the Master, we are players in your show.
Whatever understanding you give, O Lord and Master, such words do we speak.
What are we? Little worms, tiny insects; you are the great Being, the greatest of all.
We cannot tell your state or your extent, O God; how can we, the unfortunate, meet you?
O Lord God, my Master, show mercy, that we may be joined to the service of the Lord, Har Har.
Make Nanak the servant of your servants, O God, that we may keep telling of the Lord. ॥4॥
667.2: Raag Dhanasari, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
The Lord's Sant is the True Guru, the true Being, who speaks the Bani of the Lord, Har Har.
Whoever speaks it or hears it is set free; I am ever a sacrifice to him (the Guru).
O Sants of the Lord, listen with your ears to (his) praise.
Listen to the telling of the Lord, Har Har, even for an instant, a moment, and all sins and misdeeds are washed away.
Those who have found such a Sant, the Saadh (the Guru), are great, the greatest of beings.
O God, my Master, we beg for the dust of their feet; O Lord, a deep longing (for it) has taken hold of us.
O God, my Master, the Lord, Har Har, is a tree that bears fruit; those who have repeated (his Name) are satisfied.
Drinking the Amrit of the Lord, Har Har, they are fulfilled; all their hunger is gone.
Those whose fortune is great, lofty and high, have repeated the Lord's Name.
O Lord God, my Master, unite (me) with their company; servant Nanak is the slave of their slaves. ॥4॥
667.3: Raag Dhanasari, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
We are blind, utterly blind, steeped in the poison of the senses' objects; how can we walk in the Guru's way?
May the True Guru, the Giver of peace, show kindness and attach us to the hem of his robe.
O Gursikh friends, walk in the Guru's way.
Whatever the Guru says, take that as good; the telling of the Lord, Har Har, is unlike any other.
Listen, O Sants of the Lord, O brothers: serve the Guru, quickly, without delay.
Serving the True Guru, tie up the Lord('s Name) as provisions for the journey; do not reckon on today or tomorrow.
O Sants of the Lord, repeat the Lord's Name; the Lord's Sant walks with the Lord (in step with his will).
Those who have repeated the Lord have become the very form of the Lord; the Lord, the Player of wondrous plays, has met them.
I long to repeat the Lord, Har Har; O Lord, O Banwali, show mercy.
O Lord, unite servant Nanak with the Saadh Sangat; may we be the dust of the feet of the holy. ॥4॥
668.1: Raag Dhanasari, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
The Lord, Har Har, the Lord and Master, has become the raindrop (for me); I am the chatrik (rain-bird), crying out and crying out.
O Lord God, Har Har, show your mercy; O Lord, put (that drop) in my mouth, even for an instant.
Without the Lord I cannot live even for a moment.
As the addict dies without his drug, so without the Lord I die.
You, O Lord, are a pool beyond all depth; we cannot find even a trace of your limit.
You are beyond, beyond, beyond the farthest, O Master; you alone know your own state and extent.
The Lord's Sants who have repeated (the Name of) the Lord are dyed in the Guru's deep crimson (love).
Devotion to the Lord, Har Har, has taken shape (in them), and great is their glory; repeating the Lord, they have won the highest honour.
He himself is the Master, he himself the servant; he himself makes the way (of devotion).
Servant Nanak is in your refuge; O Lord, keep the honour of your devotees. ॥4॥
668.2: Raag Dhanasari, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
Tell (me), O brother, the dharma of Kalyug: how may we, who long to be free, be set free?
Repeating the Lord, Har Har, is the boat, the Lord is the raft; one who has repeated the Lord swims and crosses over.
O dear Lord, keep the honour of your servant.
Have (me) repeat your own Name, Har Har; I have asked for devotion alone.
Those servants of the Lord are dear to the Lord who have repeated the Lord through the (Guru's) word.
The account that Chitr and Gupt had written, the whole balance owed to Jam, is cleared.
The Lord's Sants have repeated the Lord, Har Har, in their minds, joining the company of the holy;
the blazing sun, the fire of craving, is put out (in them), and the moon of Shiv, the auspicious One, has risen with its cool light.
You are the great Being, great, inaccessible, beyond the senses; you yourself are all, by yourself.
O God, be gracious to servant Nanak; make (him) a slave of your slaves' slaves. ॥4॥
668.3: Raag Dhanasari, Ghar 5, Dupade, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Enshrining (him) in the heart and dwelling on (him), one repeats Murari, Ram and Ram alone, the Name of the Enticer of the mind,
(in whom) the perfect Guru has revealed the Master, unseen, beyond the senses, beyond the farthest.
The Lord (Ram) is the paaras and the sandalwood; we are wood and iron.
When (we) came into the true company (Satsang) of the Lord, of Hari, the Lord made (us) gold and sandalwood.
(Some) recite the nine (grammars) and the six (Shastras) by heart; my Lord God is not pleased this way.
Says servant Nanak: meditate on the Lord in the heart always; in this way my Lord God is pleased. ॥2॥
668.4: Raag Dhanasari, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
Speak (his) virtues, seek the Lord, serve the True Guru: meditate in this way on the Name of the Lord, Har Har.
You will be pleasing in the Lord's court, you will not come into birth again, you will merge in the Light of the Lord, Har Har Har.
O mind, repeat the Lord's Name, and you will be at peace in every way.
The Lord's praise is lofty, above all else; serve the Lord, Har Har Har, and (that service) sets you free.
When the Lord, the treasure of mercy, showed (mercy), the Guru gave the Lord's devotion; then love for the Lord came about.
Many cares are forgotten, the Lord's Name is enshrined in the heart; O Nanak, the Lord has become the companion. ॥2॥
669.1: Raag Dhanasari, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
Read the Lord, write the Lord, repeat the Lord, sing the Lord: the Lord carries (you) across the terrifying world-ocean.
In mind, in word and in heart meditate on the Lord, and, content, utter in this way the Name of the Lord, Murari.
In the mind one should repeat (the Name of) the Lord, the Master of the world,
joining the company of the Saadh (the Guru), O friend.
Bliss abides always, day and night, (if you) sing the praise of the Lord, Banwari.
When the Lord, Har Har, cast his glance (of grace), then the urge arose in the mind; (we) repeated the Name of the Lord, Har Har, and our liberation came about.
Keep the honour of servant Nanak, O my Master; O Lord, he has come and fallen at your refuge. ॥2॥
669.2: Raag Dhanasari, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
The eighty-four Siddhas, the Buddhas, the thirty-three crore (gods) and the silent sages, all of them long for your Name, O dear Lord.
By the Guru's grace some rare one obtains it: those on whose foreheads love (for the Name) was written from the very start.
O mind, repeat the Name of Ram alone; the Lord's praise is the most exalted deed.
Those who sing and hear your praise, O Master: to them I am ever a sacrifice.
O Lord and Master, Cherisher of those who come to your refuge, what you give, that alone do I receive.
O merciful to the meek, in your mercy grant (it): Nanak longs for the Lord's Simran (remembrance). ॥2॥
669.3: Raag Dhanasari, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
Servants and Sikhs all come (to the Guru's door) to worship, and all sing the sublime Bani of the Lord, Har Har;
(but) the Lord accepts the singing and hearing of those who have accepted the True Guru's command as true, wholly true.
O brothers, utter the praises of the Lord; the Lord is the tirath, the crossing over the world-ocean.
At the Lord's door those are held in high regard, O Sants, who have come to know the telling of the Lord.
He himself is the Guru, and he himself the disciple; the Lord God himself is the doer of wondrous plays.
O servant Nanak, he alone will meet the Lord whom (the Lord) himself unites; leave all else: that (praise) alone pleases the Lord. ॥2॥
669.4: Raag Dhanasari, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
The Lord fulfils desires and gives every peace; the Kamdhenu (the cow that grants every wish) is in his power.
On such a Lord one should meditate, O my soul; then you will find every peace, O my mind.
O mind, repeat Sat Naam, the True Name; ever (repeat) Sat Naam.
Here and hereafter the face shines bright, (if) one meditates daily on the Lord, the all-pervading Being, the Immaculate.
Where the Lord's Simran has come about, every trouble has gone from there; by great fortune is the Lord repeated.
The Guru has given servant Nanak this understanding: by repeating the Lord, the world-ocean is crossed. ॥2॥
670.1: Raag Dhanasari, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
O my King, may the joy of seeing the Lord be mine.
My pain you know, O King; what could anyone else know of it?
You are the True Master, the eternal One, O my King; whatever you do is all true.
Whom can one call false, O King? There is no second at all.
You are at work in all, O King; day and night, all meditate on you.
From you alone do all beg, O my King; you alone bestow gifts on all.
Everyone is within you, O my King; there is none outside you.
Every being is yours, you are everyone's, O my King; in you alone all are absorbed.
Everyone's hope is you, O my Beloved; on you alone all meditate, O my King.
As it pleases you, so keep (me), O my Beloved; you are the True One, O Emperor of Nanak. ॥4॥
670.2: Raag Dhanasari, Ghar 1, Chaupade, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
O Destroyer of the round of births, Breaker of sorrows, O Master, Lover of devotion, O Formless One,
millions of offences are wiped out in an instant when one, through the Guru, cherishes the Naam.
My mind is attached to the beloved Lord (Ram).
God, merciful to the meek, has shown mercy, and has brought the five enemies (lust, anger, greed, attachment and pride) under control.
Lovely is your place, lovely your form; your devotees shine in your court.
O Master, Giver to all beings, in your mercy save (me).
Your colour is not seen, your form cannot be made out; who can reckon your power?
You pervade the water, the land and the sky, every place, O Girdhari, of inaccessible form.
All your servants sing your praises; you are the imperishable, all-pervading Being, O Murari.
As it pleases you, so keep (me), O Master; servant Nanak is in your refuge, at your door. ॥4॥
670.3: Raag Dhanasari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Without water the fish gives up its life, for it has grown to love the water;
for love of the lotus the bumblebee perishes, for it finds no way to get out.
Now, O mind, love has been formed with the One alone,
who neither dies nor departs, and is ever with (us); (he) is recognised through the True Guru's Shabad.
For lust the elephant is caught and trapped; the poor creature falls into another's power;
for love of a sound the deer gives up its head; for that very love it is slain.
Seeing his family, the mortal is lured by greed and clings to Maya;
he is utterly absorbed (in it) and has made it his own, (yet) he must surely leave it and go.
One who loves any other than Gobind: know that he is ever miserable.
Says Nanak: the Guru has made (me) understand this: in the love of God there is joy forever. ॥4॥
671.1: Raag Dhanasari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
In his grace (the Lord) has given me the Naam, and set (me) free from (my) bonds;
all worldly entanglement has slipped from (my) mind; (he) has joined (me) to the Guru's feet.
In the Saadh Sangat I have let go of the anxious hope placed in others;
the proud intellect, attachment and the mind's cravings I have buried in a pit I dug.
No one remains my enemy, nor am I the enemy of anyone;
God (Brahm) has spread out this expanse, (and is) within (all); this understanding I have gained from the True Guru.
I have made every one my own friend, and I am a friend to all.
The separation in (my) mind has fled far away; then my King united (me with himself).
Stubbornness has perished, the Amrit has come to dwell (within), and the Guru's Shabad tastes sweet.
Nanak has seen the all-pervading Lord (Ramaiya) dwelling in all, in water, land and sky. ॥4॥
671.2: Raag Dhanasari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Since I met with the sight of the Saadh (the Guru), those blessed days have come
(in which,) singing Kirtan, there is ever great bliss, and (I) have found the all-pervading Creator.
Now I have sung the praise of Ram in my mind;
light has dawned, there is lasting peace in (my) mind: (I) have found the Perfect True Guru.
The Treasure of virtues has come to dwell within (my) heart, and so pain, doubt and fear have fled;
the thing beyond the reach of the senses has been obtained, and (my) love is fixed on Ram's Name.
Anxiety has turned to freedom from anxiety, brooding to freedom from brooding; sorrow, greed and attachment are spent.
By (his) grace the ills of Haumai are erased, and (we) have become fearless of Jam.
Attending on the Guru, serving the Guru, the Guru's command: (these) are pleasing (to me).
Says Nanak, I am a sacrifice to the Guru who has pulled (us) out from Jam. ॥4॥
671.3: Raag Dhanasari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
He to whom body, mind and wealth belong, everything is his; he alone is skilful and wise.
He alone has heard my pain and my joy, and then my state has turned good.
What the soul asks is heeded by the One alone;
(people) have worn themselves out making many other efforts, (but) their worth is not reckoned even as a sesame seed's.
The Naam, the Amrit, the priceless diamond: the Guru has given (it to me) as a mantra;
it does not fall away, nor waver; it has settled firm, and (I), made whole, am content.
Those (divides) of me and you that stood somewhat between (us): even the talk of them has vanished.
Ornaments, melted together, have become one lump, and so it is spoken of as gold.
The Light has shone forth; there are Sahaj, peace and glory; the unstruck (Anhad) Bani sounds (within).
Says Nanak, (I) have built an unshakeable home; the Guru has made (its) arrangement. ॥4॥
672.1: Raag Dhanasari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The greatest of kings and the lords of the land: their thirst has not been quenched;
drunk with Maya's pleasures, they cling (to it); (their) eyes see nothing (else).
In the poison of Maya no one has ever found contentment.
As fire is never sated by fuel, how can (one) be content without the Lord?
Day after day one eats meals of many dishes, yet his hunger is not ended;
he strives like a dog, and searches through all four quarters.
The lustful lecher may have many women, yet his eyeing of others' homes does not stop;
day after day he does (wrong), does it again, and repents; in grief and greed he withers away.
The Name of the Lord, Har Har, is boundless and priceless, the one treasure of Amrit.
Peace, Sahaj and bliss dwell in (the hearts of) the Sants; O Nanak, (this) is known through the Guru. ॥4॥
672.2: Raag Dhanasari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Nothing that this (mortal) runs after again and again can come near (this Amrit);
the one to whom the Guru has given this Amrit, it graces him alone.
The one who has come to taste the One relish
has no hunger for food and drink, or any other, dwelling in his mind.
The mind of the one who has received a single drop (of it) has blossomed, and (his) body has turned green;
I cannot describe his praise; his worth cannot be told.
It was not won by toil, nor by service; it came and was found, unlooked for.
The one on whom my Master showed mercy has practised the Guru's teaching.
(He is) merciful to the meek, ever kind, the sustainer of all beings;
like warp and weft, Gopal is blended with Nanak, as a mother with her child. ॥4॥
672.3: Raag Dhanasari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
I am a sacrifice to my own Guru, who has made the Name of the Lord, Har Har, firm within (me);
who, in the great wilderness and the darkness, has shown (me) the straight path.
Gopal, Gobind, is our breath of life,
who, here and hereafter, takes thought for all our needs.
By remembering him come all treasures, honour, greatness and full respect;
taking his Name, millions of sins are destroyed; the devotees, every one, long for the dust (of his feet).
If anyone wants all his heart's wishes, he should serve the One, the Treasure.
Remembering the Supreme Lord, the infinite Master, one crosses over.
(I) have found coolness, calm and great peace; in the company of the Sants (my) honour has been kept covered.
Gathering the Lord's wealth, the Lord's Name as food: this Nanak has made his delicacy. ॥4॥
673.1: Raag Dhanasari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The deeds that will put you to shame, that very way you have practised:
slandering the Sant and honouring the Saakat; such a perverse way you have held fast.
Lost in attachment to Maya, you have strayed into love of another.
The city of Harichand, the green leaves of the forest: such, O brother, is your worth.
Sandal paste is smeared on the body, (yet) the donkey's pleasure is in the company of ashes;
(so) you have no taste for the Amrit; (your) love is for the swindler's drug of the senses' pleasures.
The noble Sants are met by good fortune; in this world (they) are pure and holy.
The treasure of (your) birth is going in vain, won away in exchange for glass.
The sins and sorrows of birth after birth fled, (when) the Guru put the collyrium of wisdom in (the) eyes;
in the Saadh Sangat (a person) has come out of these sorrows; O Nanak, (there is now) love for the One. ॥4॥
673.2: Raag Dhanasari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Before the Sants may I carry water, wave the fan and grind (the corn), and sing the praise of Govind's virtues;
with every breath may (my) mind remember the Naam, and may (I) find this treasure of rest.
give me such understanding, my Master, that I may meditate on you for ever and ever.
By your grace may attachment and pride let go of (me), and (my) wandering be destroyed;
the One whose form is bliss pervades all; wherever I go and look, (he is there).
You are kind and merciful, a treasure of grace, O Gosain (Lord of the world), purifier of the fallen;
millions of joys, bliss and kingdoms are gained when, even for an instant, I speak (your Name) aloud.
Only that chanting, austerity and devotion is complete which is pleasing to God's mind.
Repeating the Naam, all thirst is quenched; Nanak is sated and fulfilled. ॥4॥
673.3: Raag Dhanasari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
She (Maya) who has brought under her sway the worlds of the three qualities, the world of the four quarters,
and has shattered sacrifices, holy baths, austerities and sacred places: what (can) this poor creature (do)?
When (I) took hold of God's shelter, then (I) was set free;
by the grace of the Saadh (the Guru), (I) sang of the Lord, Har Har Har, and then the sickness of the senses' pleasures ended.
She cannot be heard, no mouth of hers speaks, and as she bewitches she is never seen;
(yet) she slips in such a swindler's drug and leads (all) astray that she seems sweet to every mind.
Mother, father, son, friend, brother: in every home she has mixed in division;
with one there is more, with another less; all fight and fight to death.
I am a sacrifice to my own True Guru, who has let (me) see this play:
the world burns in a hidden fire, (but) Maya does not take hold of the devotees.
By the Sant's grace (I) have found great peace, and all bonds are cut;
Nanak has found the Name of the Lord, Har Har, as (his) wealth, and, having earned it, has brought it to his own home. ॥5॥
673.4: Raag Dhanasari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
You are the Giver, the Master, the Sustainer, our Leader and our Lord;
every instant you alone sustain (us); we children live by your support.
With (but) one tongue, which of (your) virtues can be told?
O countless, endless Lord, no one has found your end.
You destroy our millions of wrongs, and instruct (us) in many ways;
we are ignorant, of small and meagre understanding; you keep to your own age-old way.
(We are) in your refuge, (our) hope is in you; you alone are (our) friend, the giver of comfort.
Protect (us), O merciful Protector; says Nanak, (we are) the slaves of your house. ॥3॥
674.1: Raag Dhanasari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Worship, fasts, tilak marks, ritual baths, much giving of alms and charity:
by none of these disciplines is the Master won, (though people) speak sweet words.
Repeating the Name of God, the mind is at rest;
all search for him in many ways, (but he is) hard (to reach), and cannot be won.
Chanting, austerities, wandering over the earth, austerities done upside down, taking (the breath) up into the sky (the tenth door):
by these ways the Master is not won over, (nor) by the practice of Yoga, (nor by that of) the Jains.
The Naam, the Amrit, the priceless praise of the Lord: he alone has obtained it on whom (God's) grace rests.
Those servants who in the Saadh Sangat have met God in love, O Nanak, pass the night (of life) in peace. ॥3॥
674.2: Raag Dhanasari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(One who) frees (me) from bonds, unites (me) with God and recites (to me) the Name of the Lord, Har Har,
(who) makes this mind steady and still, so that it never runs anywhere again:
is there any such friend of mine?
(To him) I would give all my goods, my life and my heart; I would offer up my consciousness.
Others' wealth, others' bodies, slander of others: may (my) love not cling to these;
(may I have) the company of the Sants and converse with the Sants, (and may my) mind stay awake in the Lord's Kirtan.
O Treasure of virtues, merciful, all-pervading God, O kind (giver) of all comforts,
Nanak begs the gift of your Name, O Gopal, as a child (asks) of its mother. ॥3॥
674.3: Raag Dhanasari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The Lord, Har Har, has saved (his) Sants;
whoever wishes harm to the Lord's servant, him in turn (the Lord) strikes down.
(The Lord) himself has become the helper of his servant; the slanderers have fled, defeated;
wandering and wandering, they died there, (and) never again (came) into (their) home.
Nanak has fallen into the refuge of the Destroyer of pain, and ever sings the praises of the Infinite One;
the slanderer's face has been blackened in the court of both the next world and this. ॥2॥
674.4: Raag Dhanasari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Now (I) have called to mind the Lord, the Protector;
(he) has made the fallen pure in an instant, and destroyed all disease.
In the company of the Saadh (the Guru) the meeting came about, and lust, anger and greed were slain;
remembering the perfect Narayan again and again, (I) have carried all (my) companions across.
O mind, the One (God's Name) is the root of all medicines and mantras; (I) have set (my) faith in God within (my) mind.
Nanak ever longs for the dust of (his) feet, and is a sacrifice (to him) again and again. ॥2॥
675.1: Raag Dhanasari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
My love has become fixed on Ram.
My True Guru is ever my helper, who has cut down the very banner (Ketu) of pain.
Giving (his) hand, (he) has saved (me), and, making (me) his own, wiped out all (my) pain;
(he) has blackened the faces of the slanderers; he himself is the helper of his servant.
The True Master has become (their) protector; he has saved (them), clasping (them) to his bosom;
O Nanak, singing the Lord's praises, (they) have become fearless, and ever enjoy peace. ॥2॥
675.2: Raag Dhanasari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Your Name, O Merciful One, is the medicine.
I, the afflicted, have not known your state; (still) you yourself cherish (me).
Show grace, my Master, and take away the love of another;
cut (our) bonds and make (us) your own, so that (we) may never come back defeated.
Having fallen into your refuge, I live; you are the all-powerful, all-pervading, merciful (Lord).
At all hours may I worship God; Nanak is ever a sacrifice (to him). ॥2॥
675.3: Raag Dhanasari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
