Nothing at all can be done by us, my Lord; in your mercy, grant (us) your Name.
The world is an ocean ablaze with the fire of (attachment to) family;
(over it) lies the darkness of doubt, attachment and ignorance.
(The soul is) now high, now low, now in pleasure, now in pain;
(yet it is) never sated: craving and hunger (cling to it).
Raising up desires in the mind, (it takes on) the sickness of sensual vice;
the five enemies (lust, anger, greed, attachment and pride), wholly beyond taming, keep company with it.
(O God,) the beings, the world, the breath of life and wealth are (all) yours.
O Nanak, know the Lord to be ever near. ॥4॥
675.4: Raag Dhanasari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Driving away the pain of the poor, the Master himself keeps (the honour) of his servant.
The Lord is the boat that carries (us) across (the world-ocean), the treasure (of all comforts); no sorrow can touch (his servant).
In the company of the Saadh (the Guru), worship Gopal.
I can see no other discipline; by this effort pass through the age of Kalyug.
From the beginning to the end the merciful One fills all; there is none but him.
Repeating (the Name of) the Lord, put an end to (your) birth and death; remember that Master alone.
Each Veda, Simriti and Shastra tells (of him), and the devotees reflect (on him);
in the Saadh Sangat liberation is found, and the darkness (of ignorance) is destroyed.
His servant's support is the lotus feet (of the Lord), (his) one wealth and capital.
God is Nanak's support: (his) strength, (his) honour and (his) true refuge. ॥4॥
676.1: Raag Dhanasari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Searching and searching, I met the holy one (the Guru), and the perfect Guru made (me) understand
that all other ways are of no use; (so) I have meditated on the Name of the Lord, Har Har.
Therefore I have taken the shelter of Gopal;
I have sought the refuge of the perfect Supreme God, and all (my) entanglements are gone.
Heaven, the mortal world, the underworld and all the spheres of the earth are gripped by Maya.
Meditate on the Name of the Lord, Har Har, which saves the soul and carries all (its) lineage across.
O Nanak, as the Name of the stainless Lord (Niranjan) is sung, all treasures are found;
(but) only a rare one, to whom the Master in his mercy gives (this gift), has known (it). ॥3॥
676.2: Raag Dhanasari, Ghar 2, Chaupade, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
(Those caught in Maya) busy themselves with straw, (with things) they leave behind when they go;
(they cling to) entanglements that are of no use (to them);
they love those who will not go along with them,
and those who are enemies they take for friends.
In such doubt the world has gone astray;
the fool is losing the precious gift of human birth.
Truth and dharma he cannot bear even to look upon;
taking falsehood and fraud for sweet, he is wrapped up in them.
He loves the gift and has forgotten the Giver;
the poor wretch has no thought of death.
He rises up and weeps for what belongs to another,
and squanders all his duty and dharma.
He does not understand the Hukam (God's will), (so his) comings and goings (in birth and death go on);
he commits sins, and then (comes) remorse.
(O God,) whatever pleases you is accepted;
I am a sacrifice to your will.
Humble Nanak is your bondsman, your servant;
God, my Master, keeps (him) safe. ॥4॥
676.3: Raag Dhanasari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
For me, the meek, God's Name is the support;
for earning, (my) livelihood is (the Name of) the Lord, Har Har;
for storing up, (I have) the Lord's Name alone;
(for whoever gathers it,) it is of use to him in this world and the next.
Imbued with the Naam, in the love of the infinite God,
the holy sing the virtues of the One, the Formless Lord.
The glory of the holy one is deep humility;
the Sant has known the Lord's praise to be (his) greatness.
In the hearts of the Sants, devotion to Govind is bliss;
in the hearts of the Sants is peace; (their) anxiety is gone.
Wherever the holy and the Sants gather,
there they sing the Lord's praise with music and verse.
In the gathering of the holy there is bliss and rest;
(but) he alone gains their company on whose forehead (the writ of) grace is written.
Joining both hands I pray
that, washing (the Sants') feet, I may speak (of the Lord), the treasure of virtues.
God, merciful and kind, is ever present (to the Sants);
Nanak lives by the dust of the Sants' feet. ॥4॥
677.1: Raag Dhanasari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Why should he fear who cherishes the Master (in his heart)?
Fearing and fearing, the wretched manmukhs waste away.
(He) over whose head stands the Gurdev (the divine Guru), as mother and father,
whose form bears fruit and whose service is pure;
he whose capital is the One, the stainless Lord,
on joining the Saadh Sangat, light dawns (within him).
The Giver of all beings fills every place;
through the Lord's Name millions of troubles are erased.
All the pain of birth and death is destroyed (for him)
in whose mind and body (the Lord) comes to dwell, through the Guru.
The one whom (the Lord) himself attaches to the hem of his robe
alone finds a place in the Lord's court.
They alone are devotees who have pleased the True One;
they have been freed from the sway of Jamkaal (death).
True is the Master, true (his) court;
who can reflect and tell (his) worth?
Dwelling within every heart, he upholds all;
Nanak begs for the dust of the Sants' feet. ॥4॥
677.2: Raag Dhanasari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
(O God,) at home and abroad (your servant) trusts in you; you are with your servant.
Be merciful, O my own beloved God, that I may repeat the Name in the Lord's love.
The servant's strength is his own God.
Whatever you do and cause to be done, my Lord, that counsel is accepted (by him).
(His) honour is the Supreme God, (his) liberation Narayan, (his) wealth the accounts of the virtues of Gopal.
O Nanak, the servants of the Lord, Har Har, (abide) in the refuge of his feet; the Sants have known this to be the way. ॥2॥
677.3: Raag Dhanasari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(They) have received all their heart's wishes from God; the Guru has held (them) to his breast and saved (them).
(The Guru) has not let them burn in the world-ocean; not one (of them) has called it hard to cross.
Those in whose minds is true faith,
beholding again and again the glory of the Master, are ever in bliss and delight.
In the refuge of the feet of the perfect Supreme God, (they) have seen the Knower of hearts face to face.
O Nanak, knowing and understanding (them), (the Lord) has made (them) his own and kept safe the tender shoot of his devotees. ॥2॥
677.4: Raag Dhanasari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Wherever I look, there (God) is present; he is far from no place.
He pervades everything; O mind, I meditate on him for ever.
He who does not part (from us) here or hereafter should be counted (our) companion;
the pleasure that perishes in an instant should be called a petty pleasure.
He cherishes (all), giving them nourishment, and nothing (of what he gives) falls short;
with every breath he takes care (of all): he is my God.
God, who cannot be deceived or pierced, who is infinite, whose form is lofty,
wondrous and beyond compare: repeating (his Name) over and over, his servants delight in bliss.
Give (me) that understanding, merciful God, by which I may worship you.
Nanak begs a gift of you, God: the dust of the holy ones' feet. ॥4॥
678.1: Raag Dhanasari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
He who sent you has called you back; come home in peace and Sahaj.
In bliss and joy, in the strain of Sahaj, sing (the Lord's) virtues, and rule an unshakable kingdom.
The Lord himself has driven off your enemies, and the calamity is past.
God, the Doer of all, has brought (you) to light before all, and (your) fleeing and running are over.
In the home the music of rejoicing plays day after day; your own Master has honoured you.
Stay steady, and never waver, upheld by the Guru's word;
acclaim rings across the whole earth, and (your) face is bright in the court (of the Lord).
He whose beings they are has himself turned them back; he himself has become (their) helper.
The Doer has worked a wonder; O Nanak, true for ever is (his) greatness. ॥4॥
678.2: Raag Dhanasari, Ghar 6, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
without the Lord no one is liberated.
O mind, do pure deeds; the Lord is the boat that carries (you) across; other entanglements will be of no use to you at all.
Service of the radiant Supreme Lord (Paarbrahm) is (true) life: this teaching the Guru has given me.
One should not set (one's) love on what has no worth at all; at the very end it does not go along.
O holy one, beloved of the Lord, worship (the Lord) in your mind and body; in his company your bonds are loosed.
Hold fast to the refuge of the Supreme Lord, (keep his) lotus feet in your heart; one should make no screen of hope in any other.
He alone is the devotee, the man of wisdom, of meditation and of austerity, O Nanak, on whom (the Lord) bestows his grace. ॥3॥
678.3: Raag Dhanasari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
My dear one, it is good, O brother, it is good, so good, to beg for the Lord.
Open your eyes and see, hear the words of the Saadh (the Guru), keep the Lord of life in your mind: all must die.
Sandal and perfume, the many tastes and pleasures you enjoy, these vices of Maya: see, they are all insipid; the Name of Gobind alone is good, say the holy.
You have taken body and wealth for your own, and have not repeated the Lord's Name even for an instant; see, nothing of riches and wealth will go with you.
He whose fortune, O brother, is good has taken shelter, holding to the hem of the Sant; those in the company of the Saadh, O brother, are not tormented by Jam.
He has found, O brother, the supreme treasure, and (his) pride is gone; O Nanak, (his) mind is fixed on the One, the Formless Lord. ॥2॥
679.1: Raag Dhanasari, Ghar 7, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Remember the One Lord, remember the One, remember the One, my beloved.
He carries (you) across the vast and terrifying world-ocean of strife and suffering, greed and attachment.
(The one who) keeps him in mind with every breath, every instant, day and night,
(who), repeating (the Name) in the Saadh Sangat without a qualm, holds (its) treasure in the mind,
(who) bows to the lotus feet (of the Lord) and reflects on the virtues of Gobind:
O Nanak, the dust of the holy ones' feet brings (him) joy and peace. ॥2॥
679.2: Raag Dhanasari, Ghar 8, Dupade, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
I remember (God); remembering him again and again I find peace, and with every breath I cherish (him).
In this world and the world beyond he is with me as my helper; wherever (I may be), he is my protector.
The Guru's word dwells with (my) soul;
it does not drown in water, no thief carries it off, and no fire can burn it.
(It is to me) as wealth to the penniless, a staff to the blind, and as a mother's milk to her child.
In the ocean (of the world) Nanak has found the Lord as his ship; the Merciful One has shown (him) mercy. ॥2॥
679.3: Raag Dhanasari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Gobind has become kind and merciful, and I water my heart with the Amrit (of the Name).
The nine treasures, the riddhis and the siddhis stay at the feet of the Lord's servant.
The Sants are in bliss in every place;
at home and abroad, the Master of the devotees (is with them); he pervades every place.
No one can come up to the one who has the Lord of the world (Gusain) at his side.
The dread of Jam is erased by remembering him; Nanak meditates on (his) Name. ॥2॥
679.4: Raag Dhanasari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The man of wealth looks on his wealth and is proud; the owner of land is vain (of his land);
the king believes the whole kingdom is his; just so, the Lord's servant leans on the Master.
If anyone keeps his own support (in mind),
(that support) acts for him to the full measure of its means, and does not hold back its strength.
(The Lord's servants) have given up all others and rest on the One alone; crying, refuge, refuge, they have come (to his door).
By the Sants' grace (their) minds have become pure; O Nanak, they have sung the Lord's praises. ॥2॥
679.5: Raag Dhanasari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
One who has taken on the colour of the Lord's love in this age is the one called a hero.
He conquers his own self, and all things come under his sway, whose True Guru is the Perfect One.
Let us sing of the Master with the love of the soul:
taking his refuge, meditating on the Naam, and merging with him in Sahaj.
May the feet of (your) servants dwell in my heart, and in their company may my body be made pure.
O treasure of mercy, give (me) the dust of (your) servant's feet; for Nanak this alone is peace. ॥2॥
680.1: Raag Dhanasari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(A man) contrives and deceives people, but the Knower of hearts knows (all).
He sins, and having sinned denies it, and puts on the garb of those free of desire.
He thinks you far away, O God, (yet you are) near.
The greedy one looks this way, and from there looks that way, and stays caught in the round (of greed).
As long as the mind's wandering is not broken, no one is free.
Says Nanak: the one to whom the Master is merciful, he alone is a Sant, a devotee, a servant (of the Lord). ॥2॥
680.2: Raag Dhanasari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
His own Guru has given the Naam to the one on whose forehead (good) fortune is written.
He makes (others) hold fast to the Naam and has them repeat the Naam; this is his dharma in the world.
For the (Lord's) servant the Naam is greatness and renown;
the Naam alone is the servant's liberation, the Naam alone his honour; whatever is to be, he accepts (as God's will).
The servant who holds the wealth of the Naam in his keeping is the banker who lacks nothing.
O Nanak, his dealing is in the Naam, the Naam is his mainstay, and the Naam is the profit he receives. ॥2॥
680.3: Raag Dhanasari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(My) eyes have become pure, beholding the sight (of you); may the dust (of your feet) fall on my forehead.
May I sing the Master's praises with ever deeper delight; dwell in my heart, O Gopal.
You indeed are the Protector, O Merciful One.
O beautiful, wise and boundless Father God, be gracious (to me), O God.
(You are) the very form of supreme bliss and joy; your words are matchless and full of sweetness.
With (the Lord's) feet in his heart, Nanak has tied the True Guru's Shabad securely in the fold of his garment. ॥2॥
680.4: Raag Dhanasari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
In his own way he feeds (us), in his own way he lets (us) play;
he gives every comfort, enjoyment and delight, and is present within the mind itself.
as a mother keeps her child, so does God cherish (us).
(O Lord,) you are friend and companion, the Master of every virtue; O Divine One, you abide for ever.
Here and there, wherever (I look), there you alone are; may Nanak be granted the service of the Sants. ॥2॥
680.5: Raag Dhanasari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The Sants of Damodar are kind and merciful; they burn up the poison of lust and anger.
Kingship, wealth, youth, body and life: all these I have offered up as a sacrifice to them.
(Those) who love the Name of the Lord in mind and body
are carried across the world-ocean, with peace, Sahaj, bliss and joy.
Blessed is that place, blessed are those dwellings, where the Sants make their home.
Fulfil servant Nanak's heartfelt wish, O Master: may he bow before your devotees. ॥2॥
681.1: Raag Dhanasari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(The perfect True Guru) has freed (me) from the mighty one (Maya), drawing me to his feet;
he has given (my) mind the mantra of the Name of the One, which neither perishes nor goes anywhere.
The perfect True Guru has bestowed (this) gift:
he has given (me) the Name of the Lord, Har Har, for Kirtan, and I have been set free.
My own God has made (them) his, and kept the honour of his devotees.
Nanak has taken hold of his God's feet, and has had peace day and night. ॥2॥
681.2: Raag Dhanasari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Seizing what is others', greed, falsehood and slander: doing just these, (the Saakat) passes (his life).
He holds sweet a false hope, a mirage (the deer's thirst); this is the prop he has set up for his mind.
The Saakat's life passes in vain,
as a mouse gnaws through loads of paper and wastes them, and they are of no use to the fool.
Have mercy, O Supreme Lord, O Master, and free (me) from these bonds.
Says Nanak: O God, you pull out the blind who are drowning, (bringing them) into the company of the holy. ॥2॥
681.3: Raag Dhanasari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
As I remember God, my own Master, again and again, my body, mind and breast are cooled.
Beauty, delight, peace, the wealth of my soul and my caste: the Supreme Lord is (all these) to me.
(My) tongue is drunk on the Lord, the home of every essence;
it is dyed in the love of its own Lord; (his) lotus feet are (my) treasure and store.
The One to whom (I) belonged has himself saved (me); such is the way of the perfect God.
The Giver of peace has himself united Nanak (with him); the Lord has kept (his) honour. ॥2॥
681.4: Raag Dhanasari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(O Lord,) all the evil ones and enemies are driven off by you; your glory is plain to see.
whoever troubles your devotees, you strike him down at once.
I look to you always, O Lord.
O Murari, be a help to (your) servant; take (him) by the hand and lift (him) out, O Friend.
My Master has heard (my) prayer, and himself has done a master's part (by me).
O Nanak, by repeating (the Name of) the Lord for ever and ever, bliss has come and sorrows have fled. ॥2॥
681.5: Raag Dhanasari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(God) has spread his might in the four directions, and placed his hand on (his servant's) head.
He has looked with a glance of grace, and shattered the servant's pain.
The Guru, Govind, has protected the servants of the Lord;
clasping (them) to his breast, the merciful, forgiving Purakh has erased all (their) failings.
Whatever (his servants) ask of their own Master, that very thing he gives.
O Nanak, what the (Lord's) servant says with his mouth comes true, in this world and the next. ॥2॥
682.1: Raag Dhanasari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(God) does not let (his servant) see a hard moment; he keeps to his own age-old way (of grace).
Holding out his hand, he shields his own, and cherishes (him) with every breath.
My mind stays fixed on God,
who is ever a help, at the beginning and at the end; blessed is our Friend.
Joys have filled the mind, seeing the wondrous greatness of the Master.
Remembering the Lord again and again, enjoy bliss, O Nanak; the perfect God has kept (his servant's) honour. ॥2॥
682.2: Raag Dhanasari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
One who forgets the Giver, the Master of life: count that one unfortunate.
One whose mind has come to love the lotus feet (of the Lord) has found the pool of Amrit.
(O Lord,) your servant has woken, in love with the Lord's Name;
every trace of sloth has left his body, and (his) mind is joined to the Beloved.
Wherever I look, there is Narayan; he runs like a thread through every heart.
As he drinks the Naam's water, servant Nanak has let go of every other attachment. ॥2॥
682.3: Raag Dhanasari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The tasks of the (Lord's) servant have been fulfilled;
in Kalyug, amid the great poison of Maya, the Lord has kept (his) honour.
As he remembers God, his own Master, again and again, Jam does not come near (him).
Liberation and Baikunth are in the company of the Saadh; the servant has found the Lord's abode.
The Lord's lotus feet are his servant's wealth, the resting place of millions of comforts.
I remember Gobind, Damodar, day and night; Nanak is ever a sacrifice (to him). ॥2॥
682.4: Raag Dhanasari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
I ask one gift of the Lord:
that I may remember your Name, and (so) all (my) wishes be fulfilled.
May your feet dwell in (my) heart, and may I find the company of the Sants;
may (my) mind not be caught in the fire of grief, and may I sing (your) praises at all hours.
The Lord's service, and repeating God's Name from the middle to the end (always): (this is) the state of well-being.
O Nanak, (one who) is touched by love for the Supreme God is neither born nor dies again. ॥2॥
682.5: Raag Dhanasari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
I ask the Lord (alone) for all things;
begging of men, one gets only toil; through remembrance of God (comes) liberation.
The sages have searched the Simritis and the Puranas, and, having searched the Vedas, they proclaim:
by serving the Ocean of mercy the True One is found, and both worlds become easy.
All the other rites and dealings there are, without the Lord's remembrance, are empty.
O Nanak, the fears of birth and death have been cut away; meeting the Saadhu (the Guru), sorrows have perished. ॥2॥
682.6: Raag Dhanasari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Craving is quenched by the Lord's Name;
through the Guru's words comes great contentment, and attention is wholly fixed on God.
May the great revels of Maya die out (in me); have mercy, O my Lord, merciful to the meek.
Give (me) your Name, that by repeating it I may live; may (your) servant's toil be fulfilled.
All wishes, kingship, comforts, delights and lasting joys (come) by singing Kirtan and repeating the Naam;
O Nanak, the one in whose destiny the Creator wrote (this) from the very beginning: that servant's tasks are fulfilled. ॥2॥
683.1: Raag Dhanasari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The Supreme Lord has taken care of his servant;
the slanderers cannot stand at all; worthless, they have been blown away.
Wherever I look, there is the Master; no one can come up to him.
Whoever slights (his) servant is turned to ashes on the spot.
The Maker has become (his) protector, he who has no end, no near shore or far.
O Nanak, God has protected his servants, and struck down the slanderers and driven them out. ॥2॥
683.2: Raag Dhanasari, Ghar 9, Partal, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
O Lord, (I have come to) the refuge of (your) feet; O Gobind, destroyer of pain, give the Naam to your own servant.
Cast (your) glance, O God, and in (your) grace carry (me) across; take (me) by the arm and pull (me) out of the well.
(The soul) is blind with lust and anger, in the bonds of Maya; countless faults have covered and filled (its) body.
Besides God there is no other protector; O Hero who shields those who come for refuge, make (me) remember the Naam.
O Uplifter of the fallen, who carries all beings and creatures across: the utterance of the Vedas has not found (your) end.
O Ocean of virtues and of peace, O Supreme Lord, mine of jewels: Nanak has sung of you, who love devotion. ॥2॥
683.3: Raag Dhanasari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Remembrance is peace in this world, peace in the next, peace at all times: so the Name of Gobind should ever be taken.
(By it) the sins committed long ago are wiped away; joining the Saadh Sangat, one who was dead (in spirit) comes to life.
Power and youth make one forget the Lord; Maya is a great sorrow: so the great souls say.
The hope and the thirst to dwell on the Lord and to sing his Kirtan: this precious gift only a fortunate one receives.
O you who are able to shelter all who seek your refuge, O Indescribable One, beyond the reach of the senses: your Name is the uplifter of the fallen.
O Knower of hearts, Lord and Master of Nanak: my Master fills every place. ॥2॥
683.4: Raag Dhanasari, Ghar 12, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Salutation to the Lord, salutation! Sing the praises of Gopal, the King.
One who by great fortune meets the divine Guru:
by serving the Lord, (his) millions of offences are wiped out.
One whose mind is dyed in (the love of God's) lotus feet:
the fire of grief has no hold on that person.
In the company of the Saadh (the Guru) the (world-) ocean is crossed;
repeat the Name of the fearless Lord, with love.
(One who remembers him) commits no fault over others' wealth, no sin, no evil deed;
cruel Jam does not come near (him).
God himself has put out (their) fire of craving;
O Nanak, in God's refuge (beings) are saved. ॥5॥
684.1: Raag Dhanasari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Satisfaction has come to one who has eaten the food of truth (the Name),
(who) has meditated on the Naam in mind, in heart and with the tongue.
This is life, (remembering) the Lord is life:
repeat (the Name of) the Lord in the Saadh Sangat: (this is true) life.
He has (as it were) put on robes of many kinds
who night and day sings the Kirtan, the praises of the Lord.
He rides (as it were) on elephants, chariots and horses
who beholds the Lord's path within his heart.
Meditating on (God's) feet within mind and body,
servant Nanak has found the Lord, the treasure of peace. ॥4॥
684.2: Raag Dhanasari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The Guru's feet are the soul's deliverance:
(the feet of the Guru) who in an instant has carried (the soul) across the vast ocean (of the world).
Someone has become devoted to rituals, someone has bathed at places of pilgrimage;
the Lord's servants have meditated on the Lord's Name.
The Master is the cutter of bonds;
servant Nanak remembers (him), the Knower of hearts. ॥2॥
684.3: Raag Dhanasari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(O God,) may the love (for you) not break in any way:
pure is the way of life of your servant.
Dearer (to him) than soul, breath, mind and wealth
is the Lord, who can set a dam against Haumai.
May (my) love stay fixed on (God's) lotus feet:
684.4: Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Raag Dhanasari, by the Ninth Guru (Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji).
Why, O brother, do you go to the forests to search (for God)?
He dwells in all, is ever untouched (by Maya), (and) abides right with you.
As fragrance dwells within the flower, as the reflection is in the mirror,
so the Lord dwells within all, with no gap between; search (for him) in the heart itself, O brother.
Know the One alone, outside and within: this is what the Guru's wisdom tells.
O servant Nanak, until one knows oneself, doubt's moss is not cleared away. ॥2॥
684.5: Raag Dhanasari, by the Ninth Guru (Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji).
O holy ones, this world has strayed, lost in doubt;
it has given up the remembrance of Ram's Name and sold itself into the hands of Maya.
Mother, father, brother, sons, wife: in the relish of them it stays wrapped up;
in the intoxication of youth, wealth and power it stays crazed day and night.
To him who is merciful to the meek, ever the destroyer of pain, its mind does not cling.
O servant Nanak, among millions, only some rare one has recognised (him), becoming Gurmukh. ॥2॥
685.1: Raag Dhanasari, by the Ninth Guru (Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji).
I do not hold that yogi to know the way (of yoga)
in whose heart I see greed, attachment, Maya and the sense of mine.
He in whom there is neither slander of others nor flattery, to whom gold and iron are alike,
who stays aloof from joy and grief: call him a yogi.
The fickle mind runs off in the ten directions; one who has made it still and steady —
Says Nanak: the man who is of this kind, know him to be liberated. ॥2॥
685.2: Raag Dhanasari, by the Ninth Guru (Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji).
Now what means shall I try,
by which the mind's dread may end, (and) I may cross the terrifying world-ocean?
Having gained (human) birth I have done no good; therefore I am greatly afraid.
With mind, speech and deeds I have not sung the praises of the Lord: this worry I carry in my heart.
Hearing the Guru's teaching, no wisdom at all has sprung up (in me); I fill my belly like a beast.
Says Nanak: O God, (only if you) recognise (your own) birad (your age-old way of saving the fallen), can I, fallen as I am, cross over. ॥2॥
685.3: Raag Dhanasari, Ghar 2, Ashtapadis, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
The Guru is an ocean, brimful of jewels;
the Sants peck the Amrit (from it), and do not stay far (from it).
As it pleases God, they peck the feed of the Lord's essence;
the swan (that stays) in the lake finds the Lord of its life.
What does the poor crane gain by bathing in a puddle?
It sinks into the mud, and its filth does not go.
The thoughtful one sets down his feet with care upon care;
leaving duality, (such ones) have become the Formless One's own.
tasting the Lord's essence, (they have gained) the treasure of liberation;
their comings and goings have ended: the Guru has kept them safe.
The swan does not leave the lake and go;
through loving devotion it merges in Sahaj.
The swan is in the lake, and the ocean is in the swan;
this is a story that cannot be told; through the Guru's words (it gains) honour.
Some one yogi (rare, joined to God) sits in the realm of Sunn;
(in that state) there is neither woman nor man: tell me, how could anyone describe (it)?
he keeps his mind fixed on the Light that pervades the three worlds,
the True One, in whose refuge are the gods, men and Naths (the masters of yoga).
(He is) the source of bliss, the support of those who have none;
through the Guru, by devotion (to him) and reflection, (one abides) in Sahaj.
(He is) the lover of devotion, the dispeller of fears;
killing Haumai and setting their feet (in the holy company), (the Gurmukhs) meet (him).
Though many efforts are made, death torments (such a one);
(such beings) have come into the world with death written (in their lot).
(he) loses the treasure of (human) birth in duality;
he does not know his own self, and wandering and wandering in doubt he weeps.
(One who) speaks, reads and hears of the One alone
(gains) patience and dharma, (and takes) the support of the Upholder of the earth;
continence, truthful living and self-restraint come to dwell in (his) heart,
if (his) mind is won over to the fourth state.
To one made pure (by abiding) in the True One, no filth clings;
through the Guru's Shabad, (his) doubt and fear run away.
He whose form and being are from the beginning, beyond compare:
Nanak begs for (him), the True One, whose form is eternal. ॥8॥
686.1: Raag Dhanasari, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
One who meets (God) in Sahaj: his meeting is accepted;
for him there is no dying, no coming and going.
The servant is (merged) in the Master, and he (the Master) in the servant;
wherever I look, there is no other.
Through the Guru, by devotion, the home of Sahaj is found;
without meeting the Guru, one dies (in spirit) and keeps coming and going.
I take him alone as Guru who makes the True One firm (in the heart),
(who) has (me) speak of the Indescribable One, (and) unites (me with him) through the Shabad.
The Lord's people have no other task;
the True Master, the True One, (alone) is dear (to them).
The mind (stays) within the body, and within the mind is the True One;
that (servant), made true, meeting the True One, is absorbed (in him).
(That) servant falls at God's feet
(whom) the perfect True Guru meets and unites (with God).
(God) himself grants the sight (of himself), and he himself watches (over all);
he is not won by stubborn force, nor by many garbs.
He who fashioned the vessels (the bodies) and poured Amrit (into them):
it is that God who has won (the mortal's) mind to loving devotion.
Reading and reading, (people) go astray and suffer blows;
through much cleverness they keep coming and going.
One who repeats the Naam and eats the food of (God's) fear:
(such) servants, through the Guru, stay merged (in God).
Worshipping stones, (bathing at) places of pilgrimage, dwelling in the forests,
wandering and wavering, (some) have become renunciants;
(but) with the mind soiled, how can (one) be pure?
one who merges in the True One: he alone receives honour.
(Unite me with the Guru) in whose being are (true) conduct and reflection,
whose mind, from the beginning and through the ages, is steady in Sahaj,
who saves millions in the blink of an eye:
in your grace, O Beloved, unite (me) with (that) Guru.
Before whom, O God, should I praise you?
Apart from you, (I see) no other.
As it pleases you, so keep (me) in your will;
so that Nanak may sing (your) praises in Sahaj, in love. ॥8॥
686.2: Raag Dhanasari, Ghar 6, an Ashtapadi, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Whatever species (the soul) was born into, in that it was entangled; it has gained human birth by good fortune.
O Saadh (the Guru), I have looked to your shelter: give (me) your hand and save (me); in your grace unite (me) with the Lord, the King.
Wandering through countless births, I have found no resting place.
O Guru, I serve (you) and fall at (your) feet: show (me), revered one, the path to Govind ji.
I make countless efforts for Maya, I hold it close in my mind; (my life) ever passes in crying mine, mine.
O brother, if only I might meet such a Sant, who would take away all my anxiety (and) attach my love to the Master.
O brother, (I) have read all the Vedas, (yet) the mind's distance (from God) does not end; the five (senses) of my (body-) house are not at rest even for an instant.
O brother, (if only I might meet) such a devotee, free of Maya, who would water my heart with the one Amrit Name.
O brother, all the places of pilgrimage (one) bathed at only left the filth of the ego-bound intellect; the Master of the house (of the heart) is not pleased by them in the least.
When shall I find the Saadh Sangat, (where) there is ever bliss in the Lord, Har Har, (and where) my mind may bathe in the collyrium of wisdom?
All the ashrams (and their duties) have been kept, (yet) the mind is not satisfied; lacking discernment, (people only) wash the body.
O brother, if only one might find such a being, the very form of the Creator, dyed in the love of the Supreme Lord, who would wash the filth of evil understanding from my mind.
(One) caught up in the rituals of religion does not love (God) even for a moment; he falls into pride again and again, (and what he does) counts for nothing.
One who meets the Guru, whose very form bears fruit, ever sings (God's) praise; by the Guru's grace some rare one sees (God) with his own eyes.
What one works at by the mind's stubbornness is not counted in the least; like a crane he sits in meditation, but, O brother, he holds on to Maya.
O brother, (if only I might meet) such a giver of peace, who would tell (me) the story of God: meeting him, our liberation would come.
Gopal, the King, well pleased, cuts, O brother, the bonds of Maya; my mind is dyed in the Guru's Shabad.
I have met fearless Gobind, and there is bliss for ever and ever; Nanak has fallen at the Lord's feet and found peace.
Fruitful, fruitful, fruitful has (my life's) journey become;
meeting the Saadh (the Guru), (my) comings and goings have ended. ॥1॥
687.1: Raag Dhanasari, Chhants, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
I go to bathe at a place of pilgrimage: (my) place of pilgrimage is the Naam.
The place of pilgrimage is reflection on the Shabad, and the knowledge (of God) within.
The Guru's wisdom is the true place of pilgrimage; it is (my) ten holy days, and ever (my) Dasahara.
I ever beg for the Name of the Lord: give (it to me), O God, upholder of the earth.
The world is sick, and the Naam is (its) remedy; without the True (Lord), filth clings (to the mind).
The Guru's word is pure, a light that ever shines; it is the true place of pilgrimage and the daily bath.
Joined to the True One, (the mind) gathers no filth; what filth is there to wash away?
Having strung the garland of (the Lord's) virtues, before whom need one weep?
One who, through reflection (on the Shabad), slays (his mind) crosses over and carries (others) across; he does not come back into the womb again.
He himself becomes the paaras, one of the highest meditation; true, he pleases the True One.
Bliss is his night and day, and true joy; he casts off pain and sins.
He has found the True Name; the Guru has shown (him the Lord); no filth is on the mind set on the True One.
Union with the Friend (the Lord) in the Sangat is the perfect bath.
The singer who sings (the Lord's praise) is made beautiful through the Shabad.
Praising the True One and trusting the True Guru, (one's) mind turns to good deeds, giving and compassion.
Whoever, in the Husband's company, is pleasing (to him) and bathes in Sahaj, for him this is the confluence at Beni, purest of the pure.
Worship the True Ekankar, the One Creator, who gives every day, and (whose gift) grows ever greater.
In the company of the Friend, in the Sant Sangat, the highest state is reached; casting his glance of grace, (the Lord) has united (one) in his union.
Everyone speaks of (him); how great can he be called?
I am a fool, lowly and unknowing; by the teaching (of the Guru) I come to understand.
True is the Guru's teaching, uttered as Amrit; in it my mind has come to trust.
(People) depart and come (again), loaded with poison; through the True Shabad, my Guru (lifts that load).
Telling (of him) never comes to an end, nor (does) devotion in (his) storehouses; he alone fills and pervades all.
O Nanak, whoever utters the True One and offers prayer scours his mind, and (sees) that True One alone. ॥4॥
688.1: Raag Dhanasari, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
I live by your Name; there is bliss in (my) mind.
True, ever true, is (your) Name; Govind is the treasure of virtues.
Through the Guru's wisdom (I know): the Creator is boundless; he who created (the world) is he who destroys (it).
The summons (of death) has come, sent by (his) Hukam; no one can turn it back.
He himself creates and watches over (all), writes (the writ) on every head, and himself gives understanding.
Says Nanak: the Master is beyond reach and beyond the senses; I live by (his) true glory.
There is none equal to you; whoever has come will go.
By (your) Hukam the account (of birth and death) is settled; (the Guru) will remove the doubt.
The Guru removes doubt and has (one) utter (the praise of) the Indescribable; (that one), true, merges in the True One.
(God) himself creates and himself takes (all) back into himself; (that one) has recognised the Hukam of the Commander.
True glory has been gained from the Guru; (O Lord,) you (dwell) in (that one's) mind, a companion at the end.
O Nanak, there is no other Master besides (him); (O Lord,) glory lies in your Name.
You are the true Creator, O unseen Maker.
The Master is One; there are two paths, and strife grows.
(He) has set both paths going; all are under (his) Hukam; the world is born and dies.
Without the Naam there is no friend; (the world) has loaded itself with poison, a burden on its head.
(One) has come by (his) Hukam, yet does not understand the Hukam; (the Lord) by (his) Hukam is the one who sets (him) right.
O Nanak, through the Shabad the Master, the true Creator, is recognised.
The devotees shine at (the Lord's) court, made beautiful by the Shabad.
They speak the Bani of Amrit, their tongues steeped in (its) savour.
Their tongues steeped (in it), they thirst for the Naam; through the Guru's Shabad they are sold (to the Lord).
Touching the paaras, they become the paaras, when (O Lord) they are pleasing to your mind.
They have reached the deathless state and lost (their) self; rare is one who reflects on (such) wisdom.
O Nanak, the devotees shine at the door of the True One; they deal in the True (Name).
Hungry and thirsty for wealth (Maya), how shall I go to (his) door?
I go and ask the True Guru, and (by his counsel) I shall meditate on the Naam.
I shall meditate on the True Name, speak of the True One, and through the Guru recognise the True One.
Night and day I shall utter the Name of the Master of the lowly, the merciful, the stainless One.
(The one for whom) the work worth doing is ordained from the source subdues the mind and himself dies (to self).
O Nanak, the Naam is the highest and sweetest relish; by the Naam craving has been put away. ॥5॥
689.1: Raag Dhanasari, Chhants, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
The Husband is beside (you), O robbed bride, yet you have had no word of (him).
On (your) forehead is written the writ (of what you) earned before.
The writ earned before is not erased; what do I know of what is yet to be?
(She who is) not virtuous, not of good conduct, not dyed in (his) love, will sit and weep again and again over (her) faults.
Wealth and youth are the akk's (swallow-wort's) shade; old age comes, and the days run out.
O Nanak, without the Name the wife her husband has forsaken is cast off; through falsehood she is parted (from him).
O drowning one, you have laid waste (your) home; walk in the love of the Guru.
Meditating on the True Name, you shall find (his) mansion and dwell there in peace.
If she meditates on the Lord's Name, then she finds peace; in her parents' home (this world) are only four days.
She goes and sits in her own home, finds the True One, and is with the Beloved night and day.
Without devotion there is no dwelling in (that) home; listen, all you people!
O Nanak, she, full of delight, finds the Husband then, (when she is) dyed in the True Name.
When the Husband is dear to the bride, then the bride is dear to the Husband.
Dyed in the love of the Beloved, she becomes thoughtful through the Guru's Shabad.
Reflecting on the Guru's Shabad, dear to her Lord, she bows low again and again in devotion.
The Beloved burns away (her) attachment to Maya, and in (his) sweetness she delights in (his) love.
Dyed in the colour of love with the True Lord, she has subdued her mind and become lovely.
O Nanak, the happy wife abides in the True One; in love with the Husband, she is dear (to him).
The bride shines in the Husband's home if she pleases the Husband.
(If) she speaks false words, (her speaking) is of no use.
She speaks falsehood, which is of no use; she does not behold the Husband with her eyes.
Full of faults, forgotten by the Husband, she is cast off; (her) night (of life passes) without her lord.
She does not heed the Guru's Shabad; caught in the noose, that bride does not reach the mansion.
O Nanak, (she who) recognises her own self merges, through the Guru, in Sahaj.
Blessed is the happy wife who has come to know the Husband.
Without the Name, the false one has earned only falsehood.
Made beautiful by devotion to the Lord, she is dear to the True One; she is dyed in love and devotion for God.
The Husband is the source of joy, ever young; dyed in (his) love, she enjoys (union with) him.
Blossoming through the Guru's Shabad, she enjoys her Lord; she has obtained the fruit that brings virtues.
O Nanak, she meets the True One and gains glory; the bride shines in the Husband's home. ॥5॥
690.1: Raag Dhanasari, Ghar 1, Chhants, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
If the dear Lord shows his grace, then one can meditate on the Naam.
(If) the True Guru is met, then in love and in Sahaj one can sing (his) praises.
Singing (his) praises, one blossoms ever, night and day, when it pleases the True One himself.
He gives up pride, Haumai and Maya, and in Sahaj merges in the Naam.
The Creator himself does (this); when he himself gives, then (the gift) is received.
If the dear Lord shows his grace, then one can meditate on the Naam.
True love for the Perfect True Guru dwells within (me).
Day and night I serve him; he never slips from my mind.
I never forget (him), and keep (him) close night and day; whenever I take the Name, I live.
When I hear (it) with my ears, this mind is satisfied; through the Guru I drink the Amrit.
When (the Lord) casts his glance of grace, then he unites (one) with the True Guru; night and day the discerning intellect is at work.
True love for the Perfect True Guru dwells within (me).
When the Sat Sangat is found by great good fortune, then the savour of the Lord comes.
(One) stays attuned night and day, and so merges in Sahaj.
When he merges in Sahaj, he pleases the Lord's mind; he is ever beyond (Maya), detached.
In this world and the next, throughout the world, (he has) honour; his mind is attuned to the Name of Ram.
He is free of both joy and sorrow; whatever God does pleases him.
When the Sat Sangat is found by great good fortune, then the savour of the Lord comes.
In the love of another there is suffering; Jam has the manmukh in his sight.
He cries alas, alas, day and night, ensnared in the pain of Maya.
Ensnared in the pain of Maya, enraged through Haumai, he passes (his life) crying mine, mine.
The God who gives (all), him he does not remember; at the end he departs in regret.
Without the Name no one goes along; he is deceived by sons, wife and Maya.
In the love of another there is suffering; Jam has the manmukh in his sight.
The one whom you, in your grace, unite (with yourself) has found the mansion of the Lord.
He stays ever with palms joined; God has become dear to his mind.
When God is dear to the mind, then one merges in (his) Hukam; obeying the Hukam, he has found peace.
Every day, day and night, he keeps repeating (the Name); in Sahaj he has meditated on the Naam.
The Name, the Name alone, is the glory he has received; O Nanak, the Name is dear to (his) mind.
The one whom you, in your grace, unite (with yourself) finds the mansion of the Lord. ॥5॥
691.1: Raag Dhanasari, Chhants, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Merciful to the lowly is the True Guru, in whose company the Lord is sung.
The Lord's Name is Amrit; in the Saadh Sangat it is savoured.
Go to the company of the Saadh and dwell on the One; the pain of birth and death is destroyed.
(One for whom) grace was written from the first has learned the True (Name); the noose of Jam is cut.
Fears and doubts have fled, the knot is untied; one never comes upon the path of Jam.
Nanak prays: show mercy, that we may ever sing the praises of the Lord.
The one support of the supportless is the Name of the Stainless (Lord).
You are the Giver, the Bountiful One, destroyer of every pain.
O remover of pain, Creator, Master of peace: whoever has come to the refuge of the Saadh,
him you have carried across the dreadful world-ocean in a single moment.
You fill every place, (seen by one who has) the Guru's wisdom as salve in the eyes.
Nanak prays: may I ever remember (you), the destroyer of all pain and fear.
Showing mercy, you yourself have attached (your own) to your hem.
I am without virtue, lowly and without a master, O God, unfathomable and boundless.
O merciful Master, ever kind, who raises up the lowly,
all beings and creatures are in your power; all are in your care.
You yourself are the Creator, you yourself the enjoyer, you yourself consider all.
Nanak prays: singing (your) praises, may I live; may I repeat the chant of the Lord, O Banwari.
The sight of you is boundless, (your) Name priceless.
Your servants repeat (it) ever, O immeasurable Purakh.
You have come to dwell on the tongues of the Sants, pleased of yourself; they alone are intoxicated with the Lord's savour.
Those of great fortune who cling to the Guru's feet stay awake always, night and day.
Ever and ever (the Saadh) utters, with every breath, the praises of the Master who is to be remembered:
Nanak prays: (give me) the dust of (such a) Saadh, O God; (your) Name is priceless. ॥4॥
691.2: Raag Dhanasari, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Those like Sanak, Sanand and Mahesh (Shiv),
and Shesh Nag have not known your secret.
In the company of the Sants, I enshrine Ram in (my) heart.
Those like Hanuman, those like Garur,
the lord of the gods (Indra) and the kings of men have not known (your) virtues.
The four Vedas, the Simritis and the Puranas,
Kamlapati (Vishnu) and Kavla (Lakshmi) have not known (you).
Says Kabir: that one does not wander in doubt
who, clinging to the feet (of the Sants), stays in the refuge of Ram. ॥4॥
692.1: From days into watches, from watches into moments, life runs down and the body wastes away;
death, the hunter, prowls like a slayer of game; tell me, what way is there (to escape)?
That day has begun to draw near;
mother, father, brother, son and wife: tell me, is anyone anyone's own?
As long as the light (of life) abides in the body, the beast (that man is) does not know himself;
he greedily craves the state of living on, and his eyes see nothing.
Says Kabir: listen, O mortal, give up the delusions of the mind;
repeat the Naam alone, O mortal, and fall into the refuge of the One. ॥3॥
692.2: For one who knows anything of loving devotion, what is there (in this) to wonder at?
As water that enters water does not come out again, so the weaver, his self melted away, has merged (in the Lord).
O people of the Lord, I am simple in understanding.
If you, Kabir, give up your body in Kashi, what favour would the all-pervading Lord have done (in your release)?
Says Kabir: listen, O people: let none of you go astray in delusion;
what is Kashi, and what the barren Magahar, if Ram is in the heart? ॥2॥
692.3: (Though one) should reach the realm of Indra or the realm of Shiva,
(having got there) by petty austerities, one will come back again.
What shall I ask for? Nothing is lasting.
Keep the Name of Ram within your mind.
at the end, none of these goes with anyone as a helper.
tell me, who has found peace in these?
Says Kabir: all else is of no use;
for my mind, the (true) wealth is the Name of Ram. ॥4॥
692.4: Remember Ram, remember Ram, remember Ram, O brother.
Without remembrance of the Name of Ram, a great many are drowning.
Wife, sons, body, house and wealth, (which seem) to give comfort:
none of these is yours when the appointed hour of death has come.
Ajamal, Gaj the elephant and Ganika did sinful deeds,
(yet) they too crossed over to the far shore by taking the Name of Ram.
You have wandered through births as swine and dog, and still you felt no shame;
why do you leave the Amrit of Ram's Name and eat poison?
Give up the delusion of rites enjoined and forbidden (by the scriptures), and take the Name of Ram.
By the Guru's grace, O servant Kabir, make Ram your loving friend. ॥4॥
692.5: Raag Dhanasari, the hymn of Bhagat Namdev Ji.
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
(People) had deep foundations dug and raised mansions upon them;
(yet) who was greater in years than Markandeya, who passed his days with only straw above his head?
The Creator, Ram, is our loving friend.
O men, why do you take pride? This false body will perish.
The Kaurav brothers, such as Duryodhan, kept saying mine, mine;
their royal canopy reached over twelve jojans, yet vultures ate their bodies.
All Lanka was of gold, (its lord) one as mighty as Ravan;
what came of the elephants tethered at his door? In a moment (Lanka) passed to another.
The Yadavs played a trick on Durbasa and reaped this fruit.
(The Lord) has shown grace to his own servant, and Namdev sings the Lord's praises. ॥4॥
693.1: I have brought the ten (senses) under my control, made free of desire; the very name of the five (passions) is wiped out.
The seventy-two (thousand channels of the body) I have filled from the pool of Amrit, and the poison I kill and drive out.
I shall not come back (into birth) again,
(for) from my heart I utter the Amrit Bani and instruct my own self.
Making entreaty and falling at (the Guru's) feet, I have wrested away the hard axe (of death);
turned around, I am now the servant of the Sants, and I stand in awe of the devotees.
I am free of this world only when I do not cling to Maya;
Maya is but another name for birth in the womb; giving it up, I gain the sight (of the Lord).
Those who worship in this way are rid of all fear.
Says Namdev: why do you wander outside? By these disciplines the Lord is found. ॥4॥
693.2: As water is dear in Marwar (the land of sand), as the creeper is dear to the camel,
as the sound (of the hunter's bell) at night is dear to the deer, so dear to my mind is the beautiful Ram.
Beautiful is your Name, beautiful your form, and beautiful beyond measure your colour, O my beautiful Ram.
As Indra (the rain) is dear to the earth, as the fragrance of the flower to the bumblebee,
as the mango is dear to the koel, so dear to my mind is the beautiful Ram.
As the sun is dear to the chakvi, (as) Mansarovar to the swan,
as her husband is dear to a young woman, so dear to my mind is the beautiful Ram.
As milk is dear to a child, as the cloud to the mouth of the chatrik,
as water is dear to the fish, so dear to my mind is the beautiful Ram.
Seekers, Siddhas and all the sages long (for him), but rare is the one who has seen (him).
As your Name is dear to all the worlds, so is Bithal dear to Nama's mind. ॥5॥
693.3: In the very beginning (the world arose like) a forest of white lotuses;
Know that it is from Krishna (the Lord who draws all) that the Lord's dancing creation dances.
First of all, the Purakh (the Primal Being) himself became manifest,
then from the Purakh came Maya;
(all this is the union) of this one (Maya) and of that one (the Purakh):
the Lord's fair garden dances like the water in the pots (of a Persian wheel).
(but) none is apart from the Master.
in every woman and man it is the word of Keshav (the Lord) alone that runs, one and the same.
Like the pots (of a Persian wheel), beings rise and sink in the world;
after long wandering I have come to your door.
I, O Lord, am Nama. O Lord,
save me from the snare of the house (of the world), the root of (the fear of) Jam. ॥3॥
694.1: O Madho, to make the fallen pure is your age-old way.
Blessed are those sages who have meditated on my Lord God.
The dust of Gobind's feet has touched my forehead,
(dust that is) far even from gods, men and sages.
O Madho, merciful to the lowly, destroyer of pride,
Nama has taken the refuge of your feet and is a sacrifice to you. ॥2॥
694.2: Raag Dhanasari, the hymn of Bhagat Ravidas Ji.
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
There is none as lowly as I, and none as merciful as you; what more testing (of this) is needed now?
That my mind may be won by your words, grant your servant this (faith) in full.
O dear Ram, I am a sacrifice, ever a sacrifice, to you;
for what reason do you not speak (to me)?
For many births I was parted (from you), O Madho; this birth is given over to you.
Says Ravidas: I live on hope alone; it is long since I saw you. ॥2॥
694.3: In my mind I remember (you), with my eyes I behold (you), and I keep my ears filled with (your) Bani and your fair praise;
my mind I make the bumblebee, (your) feet I hold in my heart, and with my tongue I utter the Amrit Name of Ram.
May my love for Gobind never grow less;
I have bought it at a heavy price, in exchange for my life.
Without the Saadh Sangat, love does not arise, and without love your devotion cannot be.
Ravidas makes one prayer to the Lord: keep my honour, O Ram, Sovereign Lord. ॥2॥
694.4: Your Name, O Murari, is (my) aarti and (my) bath of pilgrimage.
Without the Lord's Name, all display is false.
Your Name is (my) seat, your Name the stone for grinding (sandal), your Name the saffron I take and sprinkle (upon you);
your Name is the water, your Name the sandalwood; to repeat the Name is to grind it, and this Name I take and offer to you.
Your Name is the lamp, your Name the wick, your Name the oil that I take and pour into it;
I have lit the flame of your Name, and all the worlds are filled with light.
Your Name is the thread, the Name the flowers and the garland; the eighteen loads of plant life are all defiled.
What can I offer you of what you yourself have made? Your Name is the fly-whisk that I wave over you.
The eighteen (Puranas), the sixty-eight (places of pilgrimage) and the four sources of life: in these the whole world is occupied.
Says Ravidas: your Name is (my) aarti; the True Name, O Lord, is the food offered to you (bhog). ॥4॥
695.1: Raag Dhanasari, the hymns of the Bhagats: the hymn of Bhagat Trilochan Ji.
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Why do you find fault with Narayan, O foolish one gone astray?
Evil deeds and good deeds are your own doing, O dear one.
(The moon) dwells on the brow of Shankar (Shiva) and bathes in the Ganga, O brother;
in the people of its line the bearer of the bow (Vishnu) was born, O brother;
(yet) because of its own deeds the stain did not leave it, O dear one.
The lamp of the world (the sun) is his master, O brother, (he is its) charioteer, and Garur, king of birds, is his kinsman;
(yet) because of his deeds Arun is lame, O dear one.
The remover of countless sins, lord of the three worlds (Shiva), wandered from tirath to tirath and found no release, O dear one;
because of his deeds the skull did not leave (his hand), O dear one.
Amrit, the moon, the cow of plenty, Lakshmi, the wish-granting tree, the long-eared horse and the skilled (physician Dhanvantar came from) the lord of rivers (the ocean);
(yet) because of its deeds its saltiness did not leave it, O dear one.
(Hanuman) burned the fort of Lanka, uprooted Ravan's garden, and brought the herb that heals wounds to please Hari (Ram Chandar);
(yet) because of his deeds his loincloth did not leave him, O dear one.
Deeds done before are not erased (by such means), O mistress of the house; that is why I repeat the Name of Ram.
Says Trilochan: (I repeat) Ram Ji (alone). ॥6॥
695.2: Raag Dhanasari, the hymn of Sri Sain Ji.
(My) aarti, made ready with incense, lamps and ghee, (is this):
I am a sacrifice to you, O Lord of Kamla.
the bliss of Ram, the Sovereign King, is (within me) always.
The finest lamp and the purest wick
are you alone, the stainless one, O Lord of Kamla.
Through devotion to Ram, one comes to know the bliss of Ram,
(one who) speaks the praise of the all-pervading Lord, the supreme bliss.
The Lord of enchanting form, who carries (us) across all fears, Gobind:
says Sain, worship (him), the Lord of supreme bliss. ॥4॥
695.3: Raag Dhanasari, the hymn of Bhagat Pipa Ji.
The body itself is the deity, the body itself the temple, the body itself the wandering Jangam and the pilgrim;
the body itself is the incense, the lamp and the food offered; in the body itself I worship, with my offering of leaves.
After searching many lands, I have found the nine treasures within the body.
Now nothing will come and nothing will go; it is Ram's glory that reigns.
He who is in the universe is the same in the body; whoever searches finds (him).
Pipa humbly prays: (the Lord) is the supreme essence; when the True Guru is found, he makes (him) seen. ॥2॥
695.4: Raag Dhanasari, the hymn of Bhagat Dhanna Ji.
O Gopal, I am a needy one at your door;
those who worship you, you set right their affairs.
I ask for lentils, flour and ghee,
that my heart may be glad each day;
and I ask for grain from a field ploughed seven times.
I ask for a cow and a buffalo in milk,
and a good wife for the home:
these servant Dhanna asks of you and receives. ॥2॥
